items.t: What’s At Stake For Black Americans In The 2026 Midterms
items.x: The 2026 midterm elections will determine which party controls the House of Representatives and Senate, shaping what legislation Congress advances, which policies receive funding and how the federal government oversees existing programs. The party in control of each chamber has significant influence over whether bills addressing health care, voting rights, education, housing and workers' rights move forward or stall. Those decisions can have direct consequences, from access to affordable medical care to the ability of Black communities to elect representatives of their choice. The Congressional Black Caucus Foundation has identified health care, voting rights and workforce policy among the major issues affecting Black Americans in 2026. items.t: Ex-NYPD Detective Victor Romero Indicted For Murder In Koran Irvine Shooting, Still Free On $1M Bail
items.x: A grand jury has indicted retired New York City police detective Victor Romero on a second-degree murder charge in the fatal shooting of Koran Irvine on the George Washington Bridge, but he remains free on $1 million bail. Romero, 62, appeared in a Lower Manhattan courtroom Tuesday (October 27). Dozens of Irvine’s coworkers shouted at Romero as he exited the courtroom, according to FOX 5 New York . The shooting followed an alleged near-collision between Irvine’s Volkswagen Golf and Romero’s vehicle near the George Washington Bridge entrance on October 20. Prosecutors allege Romero followed Irvine’s car before pulling alongside it and firing through the rear passenger-side window. The bullet struck Irvine in the right shoulder and exited through his neck, according to NBC News . Irvine, 46, lived in Valley Cottage, New York, and worked for Con Edison for more than 20 years. items.t: ‘We’re going to fight’:Louisiana’s last majority-Black district faces new legal challenge
items.x: Louisiana ’s last majority-Black congressional district is facing a legal challenge months after a Supreme Court ruling led lawmakers to eliminate another district represented by a Black congressman. The plaintiffs behind that lawsuit are now targeting the 2nd Congressional District, represented by U.S. Rep. Troy Carter. A three-judge federal panel heard arguments Tuesday (October 27) on whether the case should remain open, Verite News reported. The challenge follows the Supreme Court’s April 29 decision to strike down Louisiana’s 6th Congressional District, represented by Rep. Cleo Fields . The 6-3 ruling found that the district relied too heavily on race, weakening protections for Black voters under Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act, BIN reported. Casey Foundation Pub­lic con­ver­sa­tions about young peo­ple and gun vio­lence can be shaped by head­lines, indi­vid­ual inci­dents and assump­tions about youth crime. The dash­board draws on Gun Vio­lence Archive data made avail­able by The Trace and helps dis­tin­guish between young peo­ple who expe­ri­ence gun vio­lence as vic­tims and those involved as perpetrators. items.t: Black-Owned Transportation Company Keeps Magic City Classic Rolling For Nearly 20 Years
items.x: An Atlanta-based, Black-owned transportation company is carrying on a decades-long family legacy while helping thousands of football fans attend one of the nation’s largest HBCU sporting events, Magic City Classic, AL.com reports. For 18 years, Vectour Group has provided shuttle services for Birmingham, Alabama’s Magic City Classic, the annual football rivalry between Alabama A&M University and Alabama State University. Led by Reginald Haslam Jr., the company’s president and CEO, Vectour Group transports more than 13,000 attendees annually, according to the outlet. Founded in the late 1970s by Reggie Haslam Sr., the company grew from a transportation operation he managed while working another full-time job into a business serving major entertainment and sporting events. items.t: 81% Of Job Seekers Rejected Without Human Contact
items.x: More than 80% of U.S. job seekers have experienced rejectio n without speaking to an interviewer, according to a new survey highlighting growing frustration with hiring practices as artificial intelligence transforms recruitment , Fast Company reports . The 2026 Greenhouse Future of Hiring Candidate Report , released Oct. 20, found that 81% of American respondents had been rejected from at least one position without speaking to a human recruiter or AI interviewer in the past year. Nearly one-third, or 31%, said it happened frequently, compared with 38% of Generation Z applicants. The findings highlight mounting challenges for workers navigating an increasingly automated hiring process. Even landing an interview does not guarantee further communication, with 45% of interviewed candidates reporting that prospective employers stopped responding. Founded in 2021 by Spelman College graduate Reagan Fresnel and Morehouse College alumnus Brian Wright, Camp HBCYouth has served approximately 2,000 students in kindergarten through fifth grade. The seven-week summer program combines academic enrichment, mentorship, and hands-on activities designed to introduce children to higher education. items.x: OpenAI is facing a wrongful-death lawsuit from parents who allege that ChatGPT encouraged their daughter to stop taking prescribed epilepsy medication before her death in February. items.t: Black Native Americans: The History Of A Shared & Complicated Legacy
items.x: Source: Photo by APIC/Bettmann/Getty Images Black Native Americans have always existed, yet their history remains one of the most overlooked and frequently misunderstood chapters of American history. Their stories are woven into the history of Indigenous nations, the transatlantic slave trade, colonialism, resistance, and the fight for freedom. But how did people of African descent become part of Native American tribes between the 1600s and 1800s? The answer is far more complex than many people realize. According to the National Museum of the American Indian, Black and Indigenous identities are not mutually exclusive. Black Native Americans are Indigenous peoples of the Americas and the Caribbean, as well as descendants of Indigenous peoples of Africa. items.t: Turn this on to stop hackers from stealing your phone number
items.x: ( KTLA ) – Your phone number is more valuable than you might think. It doesn’t just let people call or text you. It can also be the key to getting into your bank accounts, email and other important services. That’s because so many companies still send two-factor authentication codes by text message. If a hacker takes control of your phone number, they could potentially intercept those codes and use them to break into your accounts, KTLA tech reporter Rich DeMuro explains. The attack is called SIM swapping. It happens when someone tricks your wireless carrier into transferring your phone number to a SIM card or eSIM they control. AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon all offer free security features designed to help prevent this. The catch? You typically have to turn them on yourself. Here’s exactly how to do it. items.t: Up to 75% of NFL players who died had signs of CTE, new study says
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — As many as 75% of NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023 may have had chronic traumatic encephalopathy , better known as CTE, a new study from researchers at Boston University estimates. CTE is a "progressive neurodegenerative disease associated with exposure to repetitive head impacts, such as those from contact sport participation, military combat exposure, intimate partner violence, and other sources," according to the study. It is most frequently diagnosed in American football players. Researchers can identify the disease only after death, usually by examining donated brains. As a result, determining how many NFL players may have CTE has proven difficult. Most donations come from families whose loved ones had memory and behavior problems, two symptoms of the ailment, thus skewing results. items.t: GM settles $220M lawsuit for allegedly selling private driver data
items.x: HARTFORD, Conn. ( WTNH ) — General Motors has agreed to pay $220 million to settle claims that it illegally sold drivers' private data and location information to third parties. The settlement, announced Thursday, concerns allegations that GM had sold the information to data brokers, who in turn sold it to insurance companies. That private data, in part, was then used to set insurance rates, according to a coalition of attorneys general in 35 states and Washington D.C. “GM turned private vehicles into mobile insurance surveillance machines without consumer consent or awareness," Connecticut Attorney General William Tong said in a Thursday press release announcing the settlement. "GM profited from the sale of this personal driving data, and consumers paid the price in the form of higher premiums." items.t: Five arrested, three charged with murder in fatal Rockford shooting
items.x: ROCKFORD, Ill (WTVO) — Five people have been arrested and charged in connection with the death of 20-year-old Maleek Cofield, according to the Rockford Police Department. Police said on Tuesday, October 27, around 11:13 p.m., officers responded to the area of Yonge and Evergreen Streets for reports of shots fired. Shortly afterward, Cofield arrived at a hospital suffering from multiple gunshot wounds. He later died from his injuries. Officials said several vehicles and a nearby residence were also struck by gunfire. Investigators said 22-year-old Damarion Evans-Mackey, 21-year-old Aryanna Ozbirn, and a 17-year-old have each been charged with first-degree murder. Meanwhile, 20-year-old Willie McGee and 20-year-old Armonti Bryant have been charged with aggravated unlawful use of weapons. Mackey, Ozbirn, McGee, and Bryant are all being held in the Winnebago County Jail.

items.t: Trick or treat forecast: More clouds, a few showers

While much of the time will be dry, enough moisture wrapping around the system could spark a few scattered showers from time to time, mainly Saturday morning and then again late in the afternoon into the evening. Rainfall amounts look like, and widespread washouts are not expected. but it may be enough that someone in your trick-or treat group will want to keep an umbrella on hand. Temperatures remain seasonably mild, but cooler than recent times in the low 60s for Saturday, then upper 60s for Sunday. This storm system will keep the cloud cover in place for Sunday while also keeping a slim chance for a shower or two.

According to the filing, two Portland-area residents were tailed, boxed in by vehicles, and had their tire slashed by an agent after filming public ICE activity in a parking lot. The October 7, 2026, encounter occurred during a surge in local enforcement that coincided with federal social media posts promising increased focus on sanctuary jurisdictions. The organization highlighted the event as part of a broader nationwide pattern of federal agents intimidating, surveilling, and retaliating against citizens documenting law enforcement in public spaces. All West Tennessee counties surrounding Shelby saw increases in turnout over 2022, though most were slightly behind the early and absentee turnout for the 2018 elections. items.t: Up to 75% of NFL players who died had signs of CTE, new study says
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — As many as 75% of NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023 may have had chronic traumatic encephalopathy , better known as CTE, a new study from researchers at Boston University estimates. CTE is a "progressive neurodegenerative disease associated with exposure to repetitive head impacts, such as those from contact sport participation, military combat exposure, intimate partner violence, and other sources," according to the study. It is most frequently diagnosed in American football players. Researchers can identify the disease only after death, usually by examining donated brains. As a result, determining how many NFL players may have CTE has proven difficult. Most donations come from families whose loved ones had memory and behavior problems, two symptoms of the ailment, thus skewing results. Officers received the call at 10:25 p.m. on October 27 and found two wounded men aged 33 and 27. items.t: How Rappers Build Wealth Beyond the Flex
items.x: I was thinking about this the other night, just listening to some classic records while the rain hit the window. It got me reflecting on how much things have shifted. For decades, the image of success in the music industry was defined by visible extravagance. You know the look. The culture celebrated diamond chains, fleets of exotic sports cars, sprawling mansions, and designer wardrobes. And these symbols of arrival were deeply important. They represented triumph over systemic poverty and a defiant assertion of worth in an industry that historically exploited its talent. But as the genre has matured into a dominant global force, the financial acumen of its biggest stars has evolved too. Are today's top artists just cultural icons? Not anymore. From higher prices to fewer products on store shelves, one Virginia shop is finding ways to adapt. For Ben Knezic, running The Cut Butchery in Alexandria, Virginia – a Washington suburb – means offering customers a little bit of everything. items.t: Healthcare becomes key midterm issue ahead of policy changes

The legislation, signed by President Donald Trump, requires states to enforce stricter Medicaid work requirements and mandate that enrollees reapply twice a year. Policy analysts warn the loss of coverage will impact hospital systems. items.t: GM settles $220M lawsuit for allegedly selling private driver data
items.x: HARTFORD, Conn. ( WTNH ) — General Motors has agreed to pay $220 million to settle claims that it illegally sold drivers' private data and location information to third parties. The settlement, announced Thursday, concerns allegations that GM had sold the information to data brokers, who in turn sold it to insurance companies. That private data, in part, was then used to set insurance rates, according to a coalition of attorneys general in 35 states and Washington D.C. “GM turned private vehicles into mobile insurance surveillance machines without consumer consent or awareness," Connecticut Attorney General William Tong said in a Thursday press release announcing the settlement. "GM profited from the sale of this personal driving data, and consumers paid the price in the form of higher premiums." items.t: Breast cancer patients receive special care kits from Augusta Coca-Cola
items.x: AUGUSTA, Ga. (WJBF) – Some patients at the Georgia Cancer Center received a special gift on Thursday. Breast cancer patient care kits were put together by employees at the Augusta Coca Cola plant and distributed to patients on Oct. 29. Kits included wool hats, socks, and water bottles. "The patients always love to get goodies to know that others are thinking of them and the personal note, we also give another gift, pillows to our breast cancer patients," Andrea Rhoden, a breast nurse navigator. "To kind of brighten somebody's day, in the midst of chaos of their life," said Corey Holloway of Augusta Coca Cola, "hopefully this is something that will put a smile on their face, to just to feel warm inside and to make them feel better." The kits were given to patients at 14 breast cancer clinics in the Southeast. October is Breast Cancer Awareness Month. Photojournalist credit: Regynal McKie

items.x: COLUMBIA, S.C. ( WSPA ) – A new South Carolina law closes a legal loophole involving child abuse deaths. PREVIOUS STORY | South Carolina law protects abuse victims under 18 Before the change, homicide-by-child-abuse charges could only be filed when the victim was 11 or younger. Gov. Henry McMaster signed the bill into law last Thursday, expanding homicide-by-child-abuse protections to all victims under 18. If a child older than 11 died as a result of abuse or neglect, prosecutors were required to pursue murder or other criminal charges instead of a homicide-by-child-abuse charge. State Senate President Thomas Alexander introduced the bill in March 2025. He said lawmakers may not have realized the age restriction prevented prosecutors from pursuing stronger charges in some cases. “There were cases that were not able to be made, charges that were not able to be made,” he said. items.t: Patrick Stewart, stage giant also of ‘Star Trek’ and ‘X-Men’ fame, dies at 86
items.x: (AP) Patrick Stewart , the classically trained stage actor who scaled the Shakespearean canon and added gravitas to a “Star Trek” franchise and the “X-Men” films, has died. He was 86. Stewart died Wednesday in Los Angeles, following “a brief and poignant journey” with Alzheimer's disease and Lewy Body Dementia, spokesperson Kelly Bush Novak said. While best known as Professor Charles Xavier and Captain Jean-Luc Picard from the "X-Men" and "Star Trek: The Next Generation" series and films, respectively, Stewart spent more of his career onstage than in the X-Mansion or on the USS Enterprise. Besides playing everyone from Claudius to Macbeth, he often performed a one-man rendition of "A Christmas Carol" and did West End and Broadway runs of Harold Pinter's "No Man's Land" and Samuel Beckett's "Waiting for Godot" in repertoire with buddy Ian McKellen.

items.t: DoorDash to buy Instacart in $17 billion grocery delivery deal
items.x: DoorDash is gobbling up Instacart in a $17 billion acquisition that will supercharge its grocery delivery business. DoorDash said the Instacart brand name and app will remain, and Instacart shoppers can continue fulfilling orders for Instacart. Grocers can also choose to work with Instacart or DoorDash. Instacart customers will now have access to 50,000 additional stores covered by DoorDash, the company said. Instacart, founded in 2012, specializes in grocery and convenience store delivery in the U.S. and Canada. Its 600,000 “shoppers” — who are independent contractors — completed 338 million orders last year, according to company filings. Instacart has a market value of $14 billion. DoorDash, founded in San Francisco in 2013, began as a restaurant delivery business but has expanded to pet food and electronics. Operating in 40 countries, it completed more than 3 billion orders last year

items.t: Death of ‘Mad Max’ actor Richard Norton linked to peptides, coroner says
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — The death of Australian actor Richard Norton has been linked to injecting unapproved peptides , according to a new coroner's report. Norton, 75, went into cardiac arrest in March 2025 after injecting prescribed but unapproved CJC1295 and ipamorelin, according to multiple reports . "Richard's death was triggered by his injection of the peptide CJC1295/Ipamorelin," the report reads. "Richard had been taking amounts of the medication in excess of the dose prescribed by his medical practitioner. The injection caused an anaphylactic reaction which in turn led to cardiac arrest." Norton was known for his role in "Mad Max: Fury Road," "The Octagon," and more, as well as his martial arts scenes with heavyweights of the genre, such as Jackie Chan and Chuck Norris. items.t: Turn this on to stop hackers from stealing your phone number
items.x: ( KTLA ) – Your phone number is more valuable than you might think. It doesn’t just let people call or text you. It can also be the key to getting into your bank accounts, email and other important services. That’s because so many companies still send two-factor authentication codes by text message. If a hacker takes control of your phone number, they could potentially intercept those codes and use them to break into your accounts, KTLA tech reporter Rich DeMuro explains. The attack is called SIM swapping. It happens when someone tricks your wireless carrier into transferring your phone number to a SIM card or eSIM they control. AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon all offer free security features designed to help prevent this. The catch? You typically have to turn them on yourself. Here’s exactly how to do it. items.t: Up to 75% of NFL players who died had signs of CTE, new study says
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — As many as 75% of NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023 may have had chronic traumatic encephalopathy , better known as CTE, a new study from researchers at Boston University estimates. CTE is a "progressive neurodegenerative disease associated with exposure to repetitive head impacts, such as those from contact sport participation, military combat exposure, intimate partner violence, and other sources," according to the study. It is most frequently diagnosed in American football players. Researchers can identify the disease only after death, usually by examining donated brains. As a result, determining how many NFL players may have CTE has proven difficult. Most donations come from families whose loved ones had memory and behavior problems, two symptoms of the ailment, thus skewing results. items.t: Turn this on to stop hackers from stealing your phone number
items.x: ( KTLA ) – Your phone number is more valuable than you might think. It doesn’t just let people call or text you. It can also be the key to getting into your bank accounts, email and other important services. That’s because so many companies still send two-factor authentication codes by text message. If a hacker takes control of your phone number, they could potentially intercept those codes and use them to break into your accounts, KTLA tech reporter Rich DeMuro explains. The attack is called SIM swapping. It happens when someone tricks your wireless carrier into transferring your phone number to a SIM card or eSIM they control. AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon all offer free security features designed to help prevent this. The catch? You typically have to turn them on yourself. Here’s exactly how to do it. items.x: KINSTON, N.C. (WNCT) A fraud investigation at a Kinston bank has led to an arrest. On Thursday, October 29, Kinston Police Department (KPD) officers responded to First Citizens Bank about an in-progress fraud. Bank employees reported that someone was attempting to withdraw $10,000 from a customer's account by using fraudulent identification. Officers were able to confirm the identification was fraudulent and took 64-year-old Willie White into custody. items.t: Up to 75% of NFL players who died had signs of CTE, new study says
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — As many as 75% of NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023 may have had chronic traumatic encephalopathy , better known as CTE, a new study from researchers at Boston University estimates. CTE is a "progressive neurodegenerative disease associated with exposure to repetitive head impacts, such as those from contact sport participation, military combat exposure, intimate partner violence, and other sources," according to the study. It is most frequently diagnosed in American football players. Researchers can identify the disease only after death, usually by examining donated brains. As a result, determining how many NFL players may have CTE has proven difficult. Most donations come from families whose loved ones had memory and behavior problems, two symptoms of the ailment, thus skewing results. items.t: Impact of holidays for Lenoir County program helping with food insecurity
items.x: KINSTON, N.C. (WNCT) As you turn your clocks and flip your calendars this weekend, don't forget that means the holiday season will soon be upon us. The same can be said for a soup kitchen that's been serving meals every day since 1984. Executive Director of Mary's Kitchen, Richard Crumbacker, said the holidays actually cut the number of meals served in half, with some daily counts of people showing up in October being as large as 200. "A lot of them will supplement their incomes, and come here and bring their families," Crumbacker said. "It's just rough times." Always in need of volunteers and a large walk-in freezer, Mary's Kitchen continues to serve despite the time of year or weather for those willing to make the trip here in a warm meal.

items.x: WASHINGTON, D.C. (WNCT) The Department of Justice announced Thursday they have brought charges against 18 people in North Carolina, including a woman residing in Duplin County, for illegally voting in the 2024 Election. According to the DOJ, Jacqueline Brown, 63, is charged with falsely claiming citizenship to vote and voting by an alien. The department said Brown is a native of Singapore, citizen of the United Kingdom, and a lawful permanent resident of the United States residing in Duplin County. She registered to vote in 2020 and voted in the 2024 general election The charges of falsely stating or claiming U.S. citizenship to vote carries a maximum penalty of five years in prison and a $250,000 fine. Voting by an alien carries a maximum penalty of one year in prison and a $100,000 fine. The DOJ said they now have charged 30 people in the state this year for illegally voting.

items.t: Federal Reserve’s preferred measure of inflation rose slightly in September
items.x: ( The Hill ) Inflation increased slightly in September after declining in August , new data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis showed Thursday. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index , the preferred inflation metric for the Federal Reserve, rose by 0.5 percent last month and was up 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland projected PCE inflation for last month at 0.5 percent month-over-month and 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. Annual inflation, according to the PCE, previously dipped from 3.7 percent in July to 3.4 percent in August. The price of gas and other energy goods rose by 9.2 percent from August to September, after increasing by 4.4 percent from July to August. items.x: FAYETTEVILLE, N.C. ( WNCN ) — As construction and underground utility work continue across North Carolina, firefighters are preparing for a dangerous emergency that can turn deadly in seconds: a collapsed trench. Dozens of firefighters from across the state, including Apex and Wilmington, gathered in Fayetteville for two days of specialized trench rescue training at Fayetteville Technical Community College. The twice-a-year training brings together FTCC, the Fayetteville Fire Department and North Carolina Urban Search and Rescue Task Force 9. It gives firefighters an opportunity to earn state certification for the first time or refresh skills they’ve already learned. Trench collapses are uncommon, but they can be extremely dangerous. They often happen at construction sites, where contractors dig underground, or during utility work when crews are installing or repairing underground lines.

items.t: FDA warns cinnamon sold in NC and other 13 states could be contaminated
items.x: ( WJW ) Ground cinnamon is being recalled in 14 states just as seasonal baking gets underway. In a recall alert shared by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, SLR Food Distribution Inc. of Hicksville, New York, said it is voluntarily recalling Wise Wife Brand Ground Cinnamon because it could be contaminated with elevated levels of lead. According to the recall alert , lead can affect nearly every bodily system, though its effects depend on the amount and duration of exposure, as well as the age and body weight of the individual. Short-term exposure to very low levels of lead may not cause any symptoms, and so far, no illnesses have been reported as a result of the potentially contaminated cinnamon, according to the recall alert. items.t: Man arrested, charged with murder in 2023 deadly shooting in North Carolina: SBI
items.x: RIEGELWOOD, N.C. ( WNCN ) — An arrest was made Thursday in a deadly North Carolina shooting from more than three years ago, the North Carolina State Bureau of Investigation said. Agents said they identified 34-year-old Terrell Demond White as the suspect in the shooting and took him into custody on Thursday. items.t: Motorcyclist dead after hitting guardrail on I-85 in Durham, police say
items.x: DURHAM, N.C. ( WNCN ) — A crash in Durham on Interstate 85 early Friday morning left a motorcyclist dead, according to police. According to the Durham Police Department, 25-year-old Lorenzo Wiley of Durham was driving a 2019 Suzuki GSX-S750 motorcycle in the south lanes of I-85 near Hillandale Road when he lost control shortly after 2 a.m. A preliminary investigation shows Wiley ran off the right side of the road while at a left curve, causing him to cross over the on-ramp to I-85 and hit the right shoulder guardrail, according to Durham police. Police said Wiley was pronounced dead at the scene. According to Durham police, speed is believed to be a factor in the crash. The crash is under investigation as of Friday morning. items.x: RALEIGH, N.C. ( WNCN ) — The U.S. Department of Justice is sending federal election monitors to three North Carolina counties on Election Day to ensure federal voting rights laws are being followed. The monitors will be in Wake, Mecklenburg and Alamance counties on Tuesday, a move raising concerns among voting rights advocates about potential voter intimidation. “There is a concern that these DOJ monitors can be confused as ICE,” said Joselle Torres, communications manager for Democracy NC. “This is not a new program. What's new is the weaponization of fear with this program. So yes, it could add to the fear that voters have in this moment." The DOJ has sent election monitors to polling places for decades to protect voters from discrimination and intimidation. items.x: RALEIGH, N.C. Drought has also expanded across the Coastal Plain and northern Piedmont, with some communities seeing conditions deteriorate after recent weeks of improvement elsewhere in the state. The concern extends beyond brown lawns and dry fields. Prolonged rainfall deficits are reducing streamflow and putting pressure on water resources that communities rely on for drinking water and other needs. What happens next? The immediate concern is that continued dry weather will allow lake levels and streamflows to fall further. As of Thursday, more than 2.1 million ballots have been cast in the two weeks of early voting, including absentee ballots. That's a 36 percent increase compared to this point in the 2022 midterms. The early voting numbers so far represent 27.3 percent of registered voters. Early voting numbers nearly doubled in just a week on October 22 more than 1.1 million ballots had been cast. items.x: PITTSBORO, N.C. ( WNCN ) A North Carolina town that sustained gas line breaks, a water pipe rupture, and other problems associated with a Google Fiber vendor has halted all work and forced the company to clean up ahead of Halloween. The Chatham County town of Pittsboro, about 30 miles west of Raleigh, said that Hyper Networks, which was installing Google Fiber , was linked to two gas line breaks and a ruptured water line from Friday until Monday. Pittsboro issued a "stop work order" on Monday for the vendor for an entire week until the town could meet with Google Fiber about the problems next week, according to a Pittsboro news release. A meeting on Monday will determine if or when work can continue, Pittsboro officials said. items.t: Turn this on to stop hackers from stealing your phone number
items.x: Your phone number is more valuable than you might think. It doesn’t just let people call or text you. It can also be the key to getting into your bank accounts, email and other important services. That’s because so many companies still send two-factor authentication codes by text message. If a hacker takes control of your phone number, they could potentially intercept those codes and use them to break into your accounts. The attack is called SIM swapping. It happens when someone tricks your wireless carrier into transferring your phone number to a SIM card or eSIM they control. The good news is that AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon all offer free security features designed to help prevent this. The catch? You typically have to turn them on yourself. Here’s exactly how to do it. items.t: Up to 75% of NFL players who died had signs of CTE, new study says
items.x: As many as 75% of NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023 may have had chronic traumatic encephalopathy , better known as CTE, a new study from researchers at Boston University estimates. CTE is a "progressive neurodegenerative disease associated with exposure to repetitive head impacts, such as those from contact sport participation, military combat exposure, intimate partner violence, and other sources," according to the study. It is most frequently diagnosed in American football players. Researchers can identify the disease only after death, usually by examining donated brains. As a result, determining how many NFL players may have CTE has proven difficult. Most donations come from families whose loved ones had memory and behavior problems, two symptoms of the ailment, thus skewing results. items.t: Death of ‘Mad Max’ actor Richard Norton linked to peptides, coroner says
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — The death of Australian actor Richard Norton has been linked to injecting unapproved peptides , according to a new coroner's report. Norton, 75, went into cardiac arrest in March 2025 after injecting prescribed but unapproved CJC1295 and ipamorelin, according to multiple reports . "Richard's death was triggered by his injection of the peptide CJC1295/Ipamorelin," the report reads. "Richard had been taking amounts of the medication in excess of the dose prescribed by his medical practitioner. The injection caused an anaphylactic reaction which in turn led to cardiac arrest." Norton was known for his role in "Mad Max: Fury Road," "The Octagon," and more, as well as his martial arts scenes with heavyweights of the genre, such as Jackie Chan and Chuck Norris. items.t: Turn this on to stop hackers from stealing your phone number
items.x: ( KTLA ) – Your phone number is more valuable than you might think. It doesn’t just let people call or text you. It can also be the key to getting into your bank accounts, email and other important services. That’s because so many companies still send two-factor authentication codes by text message. If a hacker takes control of your phone number, they could potentially intercept those codes and use them to break into your accounts, KTLA tech reporter Rich DeMuro explains. The attack is called SIM swapping. It happens when someone tricks your wireless carrier into transferring your phone number to a SIM card or eSIM they control. AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon all offer free security features designed to help prevent this. The catch? You typically have to turn them on yourself. Here’s exactly how to do it. items.t: Up to 75% of NFL players who died had signs of CTE, new study says
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — As many as 75% of NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023 may have had chronic traumatic encephalopathy , better known as CTE, a new study from researchers at Boston University estimates. CTE is a "progressive neurodegenerative disease associated with exposure to repetitive head impacts, such as those from contact sport participation, military combat exposure, intimate partner violence, and other sources," according to the study. It is most frequently diagnosed in American football players. Researchers can identify the disease only after death, usually by examining donated brains. As a result, determining how many NFL players may have CTE has proven difficult. Most donations come from families whose loved ones had memory and behavior problems, two symptoms of the ailment, thus skewing results. DoorDash said the Instacart brand name and app will remain, and Instacart shoppers can continue fulfilling orders for Instacart. Grocers can also choose to work with Instacart or DoorDash. Instacart customers will now have access to 50,000 additional stores covered by DoorDash, the company said. Instacart, founded in 2012, specializes in grocery and convenience store delivery in the U.S. and Canada. Its 600,000 “shoppers” — who are independent contractors — completed 338 million orders last year, according to company filings. Instacart has a market value of $14 billion. DoorDash, founded in San Francisco in 2013, began as a restaurant delivery business but has expanded to pet food and electronics. Operating in 40 countries, it completed more than 3 billion orders last year

items.t: RFK Jr. eases access to unproven peptides despite opposition from FDA scientists
items.x: WASHINGTON (AP) — The Trump administration on Wednesday acted to ease access to unproven peptide drugs favored by Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr . Food and Drug Administration scientific staffers had little input on the decision and opposed the changes, according to six people familiar with its development. The draft policy posted online by Kennedy’s Department of Health and Human Services covers a handful of injectable peptides promoted within the wellness industry for uses such as building muscle, healing injuries and boosting energy. The government will take comments for two weeks before finalizing the measure. items.x: WASHINGTON, D.C. (NEXSTAR) President Trump says his tariffs are helping the American economy grow but for some small businesses, the math isn't working out. From higher prices to fewer products on store shelves, one Virginia shop is finding ways to adapt. items.t: Your Local Election Headquarters: Speaking with Republican nominee, incumbent Gov. Sarah Huckabee Sanders
items.x: Gov. Sarah Huckabee Sanders is Arkansas’ 47 th Governor and the first woman to serve in that role. Sanders said she is proud of what her administration has accomplished in Arkansas over the last four years, and she wants to continue that work with another term. Caroline Derby sat down with the incumbent and Republican nominee to discuss affordability right now, and tax cuts in her first term, as well as possible tax cuts to come. They discussed Education Freedom Accounts and the changes made to the state’s education system under the LEARNS Act. Sanders said she plans to build upon the program and says she’ll continue to push until Arkansas leads the nation in everything from education to public safety to healthcare. items.t: UCA Bears volleyball coach John Newberry resigns
items.x: CONWAY, Ark. – Central Arkansas Bears head volleyball coach John Newberry has resigned, the program announced Friday evening. According to a release from the school, Director of Athletics Matt Whiting announced that assistant coach Jovan Garcia has been elevated to interim head coach effective immediately. Newberry has led the Sugar Bears since the 2020-21 season, compiling an 89-95 record. The program won the ASUN Volleyball Championship Tournament in 2025 before losing to #2-ranked SMU 3-0 in the first round. "I want to thank Coach Newberry and his family for the contributions they have made during his tenure leading the Sugar Bear Volleyball program. We wish him the best in his future endeavors," Whiting said. Whiting said that a search for the next head volleyball coach will start immediately.

items.t: Arkansas State Police investigating inmate death at Varner Unit
items.x: LINCOLN COUNTY, Ark. – Arkansas State Police stated they are investigating the death of an inmate at the Varner Unit in Lincoln County. State police officials said 32-year-old Wade May told prison staff around 4:30 p.m. on Thursday that he was bleeding due to a neck wound. Authorities said May was then taken to Jefferson Regional in Pine Bluff, where he was pronounced dead around 5:45 p.m. Officials said another inmate has been identified as a suspect. According to ASP, May was serving an 84-month sentence for a 2024 aggravated assault on a family member out of Nevada County.

items.t: Leo XIV becomes first pope ever to vote in US general election
items.x: VATICAN CITY (AP) — Pope Leo XIV has become the first pope to vote in a U.S. general election. The Vatican confirmed Friday that the Chicago-born pontiff had submitted a mail-in ballot in Chicago ahead of November’s midterm elections, citing his long-standing belief in civic participation. Leo, formerly Robert Prevost, “has exercised his right to vote as a United States citizen” and has done so “whenever he was eligible to do so,” the Holy See press office said. The statement said he had also voted while living in Peru whenever he was eligible. “The Holy Father expresses his belief in the right and the duty of citizens to participate in democratic processes,” it added. Leo’s vote was first reported by the Chicago Sun-Times, which quoted the chief of staff at the Will County clerk’s office as saying the pope, registered at a New Lenox address, requested a mail-in ballot on Oct. 3. items.t: Turn this on to stop hackers from stealing your phone number
items.x: ( KTLA ) – Your phone number is more valuable than you might think. It doesn’t just let people call or text you. It can also be the key to getting into your bank accounts, email and other important services. That’s because so many companies still send two-factor authentication codes by text message. If a hacker takes control of your phone number, they could potentially intercept those codes and use them to break into your accounts, KTLA tech reporter Rich DeMuro explains. The attack is called SIM swapping. It happens when someone tricks your wireless carrier into transferring your phone number to a SIM card or eSIM they control. AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon all offer free security features designed to help prevent this. The catch? You typically have to turn them on yourself. Here’s exactly how to do it. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index , the preferred inflation metric for the Federal Reserve, rose by 0.5 percent last month and was up 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland projected PCE inflation for last month at 0.5 percent month-over-month and 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. The price of gas and other energy goods rose by 9.2 percent from August to September, after increasing by 4.4 percent from July to August. Bam Adebayo also had 24 points and grabbed nine rebounds for the Heat, who lost their first four games after acquiring Antetokounmpo from Milwaukee in the offseason. Adebayo passed Udonis Haslem to become the Heat's career leader in rebounds . Andrew Wiggins scored 18 points and Pelle Larsson had 17 points, eight assists and six rebounds for the Heat, who shot 53% from the field and had a whopping 70 points in the paint. Rookie Kingston Flemings and Nickeil Alexander-Walker each scored 23 points for the Hawks, who have dropped three in a row after opening the season with consecutive wins. items.t: Arkansas Storm Team Forecast: Clouds are starting to creep in today ahead of our next rain chance on Halloween
items.x: While clouds are moving in today, they will not bring rain, but they are part of the system that will bring our much needed rain on Saturday, Halloween. The first rain is possible Friday night with some isolated light showers, but more scattered light showers are expected Saturday morning and throughout Saturday and Saturday night as the trick-or-treaters try to go gather their candy. Another system is looking more probable for next Tuesday with not just showers but thunderstorms too.

items.t: Trump tariffs hitting small business owners in multiple ways
items.x: WASHINGTON, D.C. (NEXSTAR) President Trump says his tariffs are helping the American economy grow but for some small businesses, the math isn't working out. From higher prices to fewer products on store shelves, one Virginia shop is finding ways to adapt. For Ben Knezic, running The Cut Butchery in Alexandria, Virginia – a Washington suburb – means offering customers a little bit of everything. From fresh meats and seafood to imported wines, cheeses and specialty foods, Knezic says Trump's tariffs are making some of those products more expensive. “Just seeing prices on our goods go up and up,” said Knezic. “We've had to raise prices on a lot of things like cheese and wine and some of the other stuff we import." items.t: Death of ‘Mad Max’ actor Richard Norton linked to peptides, coroner says
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — The death of Australian actor Richard Norton has been linked to injecting unapproved peptides , according to a new coroner's report. Norton, 75, went into cardiac arrest in March 2025 after injecting prescribed but unapproved CJC1295 and ipamorelin, according to multiple reports . "Richard's death was triggered by his injection of the peptide CJC1295/Ipamorelin," the report reads. "Richard had been taking amounts of the medication in excess of the dose prescribed by his medical practitioner. The injection caused an anaphylactic reaction which in turn led to cardiac arrest." Norton was known for his role in "Mad Max: Fury Road," "The Octagon," and more, as well as his martial arts scenes with heavyweights of the genre, such as Jackie Chan and Chuck Norris. items.t: Appeals court rules against Trump — again — on California ballots

The majority comprised U.S. Circuit Judge Gabriel Sanchez, an appointee of former President Biden, and U.S. Circuit Judge Mark Bennett, appointed by President Trump. items.t: Turn this on to stop hackers from stealing your phone number
items.x: ( KTLA ) – Your phone number is more valuable than you might think. It doesn’t just let people call or text you. It can also be the key to getting into your bank accounts, email and other important services. That’s because so many companies still send two-factor authentication codes by text message. If a hacker takes control of your phone number, they could potentially intercept those codes and use them to break into your accounts, KTLA tech reporter Rich DeMuro explains. The attack is called SIM swapping. It happens when someone tricks your wireless carrier into transferring your phone number to a SIM card or eSIM they control. AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon all offer free security features designed to help prevent this. The catch? You typically have to turn them on yourself. Here’s exactly how to do it. items.x: (FOX40.COM) — Officials with the Stanislaus County Public Health are reporting four confirmed cases of mpox, also known as monkeypox, in the area. The California Department of Public Health confirmed that two of the cases are Clade I, while the other two are still being tested. Three of the people reported that they did not travel internationally, and the travel history for the fourth person is still being assessed. items.t: CHP officers search for two vehicles after fatal hit-and-run on Florin Road
items.x: (FOX40.COM) — Officers with the California Highway Patrol are searching for two vehicles involved in a Sacramento hit-and-run that left a man dead early Friday morning. CHP said officers responded to reports of a person lying in the roadway around 12:34 a.m. on Florin Road, west of 55th Street. Authorities arrived to find a man dead after being hit by a car. The investigation indicates that the man was in the #1 lane of the road when an unidentified car hit him before fleeing the scene. He was then hit by a second unidentified car, which also fled. Witnesses or anyone with information is asked to contact South Sacramento CHP at 916-897-5600. The crash is under investigation.

items.t: Sacramento man convicted of human trafficking offenses against minor
items.x: (FOX40.COM) — A man in Sacramento was convicted by a jury of attempting to commit human trafficking on a minor as well as pimping and pandering on Tuesday, the Sacramento District Attorney’s Office said. The arrest of the defendant, James Wilkerson, was a result of a joint Sacramento Regional Human Trafficking Task Force operation on July 25 this year. Prior to his arrest, Wilkerson contacted a task force undercover agent posing as a minor and asked her to be a sex worker for him as well as pay him to be her pimp. Wilkerson also stated that another female was working as a sex worker for his benefit. The task force was able to identify the victim and recover her before conducting an operation for Wilkerson’s arrest. Wilkerson will be facing a maximum sentence of 26 years and 8 months in prison. His sentencing is scheduled for Jan. 22, 2027 at 9 a.m.

items.x: ( The Hill ) President Donald Trump will hold in-person rallies in Iowa and Kansas after all, a source familiar with the matter told The Hill. The Thursday announcement that he would shift to tele-rallies in the battleground states stirred speculation about the president's reason for scaling back his midterm travel schedule. The rallies were rearranged for scheduling purposes to accommodate dozens of additional tele-rallies recently added to the president’s schedule, the source said. The Kansas rally was initially scheduled for Saturday and Iowa for Sunday. Both will now be held on Sunday. items.x: (FOX40.COM) — A worker servicing an HVAC unit at a WinCo in Modesto was taken to the hospital after falling through the roof, according to the Modesto Fire Department. MFD said crews responded around 2:26 p.m. to the WinCo Foods on Plaza Parkway after a worker accidentally stepped on a skylight and fell 50 feet to the floor. items.t: Christa Pike says she remains in constant pain after botched execution in Tennessee
items.x: NASHVILLE, Tenn. ( WKRN ) — A month after Tennessee failed to execute the only woman on death row, Christa Pike has released a statement through her attorneys. Pike, 50, said she had been "prepared to die" when she entered the execution chamber at a Tennessee prison last month. Then, after surviving the failed execution by lethal injection, she said she "woke up alone in a hospital confused and in pain." "There hasn’t been a moment since that night when I haven’t been in pain. My body hurts. My arms hurt," Pike said in the statement. "My hands hurt. My throat hurts. I still struggle to speak. And the pain isn’t just physical. There is pain in my mind and in my soul." items.t: Up to 75% of NFL players who died had signs of CTE, new study says
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — As many as 75% of NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023 may have had chronic traumatic encephalopathy , better known as CTE, a new study from researchers at Boston University estimates. CTE is a "progressive neurodegenerative disease associated with exposure to repetitive head impacts, such as those from contact sport participation, military combat exposure, intimate partner violence, and other sources," according to the study. It is most frequently diagnosed in American football players. Researchers can identify the disease only after death, usually by examining donated brains. As a result, determining how many NFL players may have CTE has proven difficult. Most donations come from families whose loved ones had memory and behavior problems, two symptoms of the ailment, thus skewing results. items.t: One person dead after Fairfield crash on I-80 involving sport bike

CHP said a person riding a BMW sport bike crashed around 4:22 a.m. on westbound Interstate 80 at the Manuel Campos Parkway onramp. The rider, identified as a 37-year-old man from Vacaville, was entering the onramp and failed to negotiate the curve due to his speed and crashed, CHP said. Officers arrived to find the man unconscious with shallow breathing. The Fairfield Fire Department began life-saving measures. items.t: Sen. Darline Graham votes in Lexington, talks campaign’s final days
items.x: LEXINGTON, S.C. ( WSPA ) – Sen. Darline Graham cast her ballot in Lexington on Thursday afternoon alongside her family. The vote follows President Donald Trump's visit to Rock Hill earlier in the day. Democrats see battleground map expand to South Carolina Graham said she spoke with the president about Russia sanctions and could speak with him again before Election Day. She said she has campaigned across South Carolina to earn voters' support. “I have worked from one end of this state to the other. I start early in the morning and I don’t end until late at night,” Graham said. Asked about not receiving support from Congressman Ralph Norman, Graham said a write-in vote is essentially a vote for Democratic candidate Dr. Annie Andrews. Early voting ends Oct. 31, with Election Day on Tuesday, Nov. 3.

items.t: Benedictine dominates Groves on senior night
items.x: SAVANNAH, Ga. (WSAV) — Benedictine football defeated Groves 49-6 on its senior night at Memorial Stadium Thursday night. items.t: Liberty County basketball ready for new classification
items.x: HINESVILLE, Ga. (WSAV) — Liberty County basketball will begin its first season in Region 3-AAAA after it moved up from Region 3-AAA in the offseason. The Panthers are coming off a solid 15-9 season where they finished second in Region 3-AAA with a record of 12-2 in region play. The success was also a big jump from the year before when they finished 11-11. Head coach Levon Grant said his team is prepared to take on the classification change. "We tend to worry about the things going on right here in this gym," said Grant. "We have a lot of juniors and seniors that made a big impact last year, and when you have that, you tend to focus on yourself." Liberty County will begin the season hosting Wayne County on Nov. 19.

items.x: HINESVILLE, Ga. (WSAV) — Fort Stewart officials unveiled a new driving training course for tactical vehicles Thursday. The course lets soldiers get behind the wheel and learn how to maneuver through the kind of challenging terrain they could face in combat. The 37-acre course started as nothing more than a field of pine trees. In less than 100 days, soldiers at Fort Stewart transformed it into a training course built from the ground up. It's designed to prepare soldiers for the unexpected while giving them a safe place to train for dangerous real-world situations. From uneven terrain to crossing wet gaps in the land, the driving range puts soldiers and their tactical vehicles to the test. "So this is really building soldiers' lethality and readiness, making them more confident in their abilities to move," said Lieutenant Colonel William Watts. State Senate President Thomas Alexander introduced the bill in March 2025. items.t: GM settles $220M lawsuit for allegedly selling private driver data
items.x: HARTFORD, Conn. ( WTNH ) — General Motors has agreed to pay $220 million to settle claims that it illegally sold drivers' private data and location information to third parties. The settlement, announced Thursday, concerns allegations that GM had sold the information to data brokers, who in turn sold it to insurance companies. That private data, in part, was then used to set insurance rates, according to a coalition of attorneys general in 35 states and Washington D.C. “GM turned private vehicles into mobile insurance surveillance machines without consumer consent or awareness," Connecticut Attorney General William Tong said in a Thursday press release announcing the settlement. "GM profited from the sale of this personal driving data, and consumers paid the price in the form of higher premiums." items.t: New SC law requires restaurants to disclose imported shrimp starting Wednesday
items.x: SOUTH CAROLINA (WCBD) A new South Carolina law aimed at increasing transparency for seafood consumers takes effect Wednesday, requiring restaurants and other food service establishments to disclose when they serve imported shrimp. The law , signed by Gov. Henry McMaster on June 30, requires establishments that serve imported shrimp to post notices on menus and at their main entrances informing customers that they may serve imported shrimp. The measure took effect 120 days after the governor signed it. Under the law, businesses that serve both domestic and imported shrimp must display a notice stating: "Some items served at this establishment may contain foreign imported shrimp. Ask for more information." Establishments that serve only imported shrimp must post a notice stating that some menu items contain foreign imported shrimp. items.t: Federal Reserve’s preferred measure of inflation rose slightly in September
items.x: Inflation increased slightly in September after declining in August , new data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis showed Thursday. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index , the preferred inflation metric for the Federal Reserve, rose by 0.5 percent last month and was up 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland projected PCE inflation for last month at 0.5 percent month-over-month and 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. items.t: Up to 75% of NFL players who died had signs of CTE, new study says
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — As many as 75% of NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023 may have had chronic traumatic encephalopathy , better known as CTE, a new study from researchers at Boston University estimates. CTE is a "progressive neurodegenerative disease associated with exposure to repetitive head impacts, such as those from contact sport participation, military combat exposure, intimate partner violence, and other sources," according to the study. It is most frequently diagnosed in American football players. Researchers can identify the disease only after death, usually by examining donated brains. As a result, determining how many NFL players may have CTE has proven difficult. Most donations come from families whose loved ones had memory and behavior problems, two symptoms of the ailment, thus skewing results. items.t: GM settles $220M lawsuit for allegedly selling private driver data
items.x: HARTFORD, Conn. ( WTNH ) — General Motors has agreed to pay $220 million to settle claims that it illegally sold drivers' private data and location information to third parties. The settlement, announced Thursday, concerns allegations that GM had sold the information to data brokers, who in turn sold it to insurance companies. That private data, in part, was then used to set insurance rates, according to a coalition of attorneys general in 35 states and Washington D.C. “GM turned private vehicles into mobile insurance surveillance machines without consumer consent or awareness," Connecticut Attorney General William Tong said in a Thursday press release announcing the settlement. "GM profited from the sale of this personal driving data, and consumers paid the price in the form of higher premiums." items.t: Joe’s Blog: Next week will be a cooler week (THU-10/29)
items.x: A very weak front is stuck right now just toward the NW of the Metro temperatures in Nebraska and SW Iowa are in the 30s and 40s while we start the day with lows in the upper 50s. As a matter of fact, it's a top 10 mildest start to 10/29 in our weather record data. Which is sort of par for the course this October, a month now running more than 7° above average, and when you start near 60° when average is closer to 40° Well, you can likely tell it will be another warm day in the region. items.t: Leo XIV becomes first pope ever to vote in US general election
items.x: VATICAN CITY (AP) — Pope Leo XIV has become the first pope to vote in a U.S. general election. The Vatican confirmed Friday that the Chicago-born pontiff had submitted a mail-in ballot in Chicago ahead of November’s midterm elections, citing his long-standing belief in civic participation. items.t: Up to 75% of NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023 had signs of CTE, new study says
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — As many as 75% of NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023 may have had chronic traumatic encephalopathy , better known as CTE, a new study from researchers at Boston University estimates. CTE is a "progressive neurodegenerative disease associated with exposure to repetitive head impacts, such as those from contact sport participation, military combat exposure, intimate partner violence, and other sources," according to the study. It is most frequently diagnosed in American football players. Researchers can identify the disease only after death, usually by examining donated brains. As a result, determining how many NFL players may have CTE has proven difficult. Most donations come from families whose loved ones had memory and behavior problems, two symptoms of the ailment, thus skewing results. items.t: GM settles $220M lawsuit for allegedly selling private driver data
items.x: HARTFORD, Conn. ( WTNH ) — General Motors has agreed to pay $220 million to settle claims that it illegally sold drivers' private data and location information to third parties. The settlement, announced Thursday, concerns allegations that GM had sold the information to data brokers, who in turn sold it to insurance companies. That private data, in part, was then used to set insurance rates, according to a coalition of attorneys general in 35 states and Washington D.C. “GM turned private vehicles into mobile insurance surveillance machines without consumer consent or awareness," Connecticut Attorney General William Tong said in a Thursday press release announcing the settlement. "GM profited from the sale of this personal driving data, and consumers paid the price in the form of higher premiums." Republican incumbent Ellen Weaver is facing Democratic candidate Sylvia Wright, an educator with more than 20 years of experience and United Citizens Party candidate Dr. Baba Amin Ojuok. items.t: Turn this on to stop hackers from stealing your phone number
items.x: ( KTLA ) – Your phone number is more valuable than you might think. It doesn’t just let people call or text you. It can also be the key to getting into your bank accounts, email and other important services. That’s because so many companies still send two-factor authentication codes by text message. If a hacker takes control of your phone number, they could potentially intercept those codes and use them to break into your accounts, KTLA tech reporter Rich DeMuro explains. The attack is called SIM swapping. It happens when someone tricks your wireless carrier into transferring your phone number to a SIM card or eSIM they control. AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon all offer free security features designed to help prevent this. The catch? You typically have to turn them on yourself. Here’s exactly how to do it. The Mauldin Police Department is at the scene at Townes at Brookwood on Stonebriar Street, where officials have confirmed that a woman is dead. items.t: Christa Pike says she remains in constant pain after botched execution in Tennessee
items.x: NASHVILLE, Tenn. ( WKRN ) — A month after Tennessee failed to execute the only woman on death row, Christa Pike has released a statement through her attorneys. Pike, 50, said she had been "prepared to die" when she entered the execution chamber at a Tennessee prison last month. Then, after surviving the failed execution by lethal injection, she said she "woke up alone in a hospital confused and in pain." "There hasn’t been a moment since that night when I haven’t been in pain. My body hurts. My arms hurt," Pike said in the statement. "My hands hurt. My throat hurts. I still struggle to speak. And the pain isn’t just physical. There is pain in my mind and in my soul." items.t: Leo XIV becomes first pope ever to vote in US general election
items.x: VATICAN CITY (AP) — Pope Leo XIV has become the first pope to vote in a U.S. general election. The Vatican confirmed Friday that the Chicago-born pontiff had submitted a mail-in ballot in Chicago ahead of November’s midterm elections, citing his long-standing belief in civic participation. Leo, formerly Robert Prevost, “has exercised his right to vote as a United States citizen” and has done so “whenever he was eligible to do so,” the Holy See press office said. The statement said he had also voted while living in Peru whenever he was eligible. “The Holy Father expresses his belief in the right and the duty of citizens to participate in democratic processes,” it added. Leo’s vote was first reported by the Chicago Sun-Times, which quoted the chief of staff at the Will County clerk’s office as saying the pope, registered at a New Lenox address, requested a mail-in ballot on Oct. 3. items.t: Arrest made after missing man’s body found buried on Laurens Co. property
items.x: NEWBERRY COUNTY, S.C. (WSPA) Officials announced an arrest Friday in connection with the death of an 87-year-old man whose body was found buried on a Laurens County property. Newberry County Sheriff Lee Foster said 46-year-old Richard Lewis Cribb was arrested in connection with the disappearance of 87-year-old Edwin Geer. Geer, who lived in the Chappells area of Newberry County, was last seen October 6 and was reported missing on October 17. Foster said neighbors noticed there had been no movement at Geer's home and mail had not been picked up and Geer's pickup truck was also missing. According to Foster, investigators determined that people had been in and out of Geer's home over a period of time, including Cribb. Cribb began using Geer's property, vehicles, and credit cards beginning on October 6, investigators said. Undated photo of Edwin Geer (Photo: Newberry County Sheriff's Office)

items.t: Arrests made in double homicide at WNC apartments
items.x: BUNCOMBE COUNTY, N.C. (WSPA) Two murder suspects were arrested in the shooting deaths of two men in the parking lot of a Western North Carolina apartment complex. The Buncombe County Sheriff’s Office arrested and charged 28-year-old Tyquan Jahlil Ward and 18-year-old Keith Harold Mooney Jr. with First-Degree Murder and Attempted Robbery with a Dangerous Weapon in the Pine Needle Apartments homicide investigation. Around 12:20 a.m. on October 24 th , deputies responded to a call of gunshots at Pine Needle Apartments in Arden. 19-year-old Joshua Sanchez Ramirez and 27-year-old Darion Armon Smith were found deceased from gunshot wounds in a parking lot. Further investigation led authorities to identify Ward and Mooney as the suspected shooters. Ward was taken into custody Thursday night, and Mooney was located in Atlanta, Georgia, Friday morning by the DeKalb County Police Department.

items.x: ( The Hill ) A suspected hack at Binance prompted cryptocurrency firms to freeze about $3 billion in assets, the company said on Thursday. The exchange, which described the situation as a "security issue," has temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals while it "conducts security checks, freezes funds, and works with law enforcement." It vowed to cover all losses. "It does look like a hack on Binance," the company's co-founder Changpeng Zhao wrote in a post on the social platform X. He touted fellow crypto firms Tether and Circle for quickly freezing funds. Zhao acknowledged he no longer manages the company but said he expects "all user funds will be fully covered." The Binance co-founder stepped down as CEO in 2023 when he pleaded guilty to violating anti-money laundering laws. President Trump pardoned Zhao in November 2025. items.x: GREENVILLE, S.C. (WSPA) The Wade Hampton Fire Department is ready for any kind of live-saving situation. Sometimes, the victims come with four legs. "As a firefighter, our main priority is life. So, regardless of the life, we're going to save it," Zach Head, with the Wade Hampton Fire Department, said. An estimated 500,000 pets are impacted by fire yearly, according to Project Paws Alive. The group says 40,000 of those animals die, mostly from smoke inhalation. The department's trucks are equipped with pet oxygen masks. "It's two parts. You have a part where you can actually breathe for an animal," according to Head. "There's another part where you can just hook it up to an oxygen tank and let the air just come straight to an animal, just to get their O₂ saturation back up." items.t: Panthers fall in Green Bay
items.x: GREEN BAY, Wis. (AP) Jordan Love threw three touchdown passes, Josh Jacobs scored twice and the Green Bay Packers withstood three turnovers to beat the Carolina Panthers 27-19 on Thursday night. Love went 30 of 41 for 288 yards with touchdown passes to Tucker Kraft, Matthew Golden and Jacobs plus an interception. Although he rushed for only 39 yards on 21 carries against the NFL’s lowest-ranked run defense, Jacobs scored on a 4-yard catch and 1-yard run. After trailing 27-10 in the third quarter, Carolina cut Green Bay’s lead to 27-19 on Bryce Young’s 26-yard touchdown pass to Jalen Coker on a fourth-and-3 play with 5:37 remaining. Young’s ensuing 2-point conversion pass was incomplete. The Panthers (3-4) got the ball back at their own 45 before losing the ball on downs at midfield with 2:41 remaining. items.t: E-bike rider dies after being struck in Spartanburg County
items.x: SPARTANBURG COUNTY, S.C. ( WSPA ) An e-bike rider died after being hit by a pickup truck Thursday in Spartanburg County, the South Carolina Highway Patrol said. Officials said the crash took place around 7:17 p.m. on Campground Road near Knightsridge Road. According to SCHP, the victim was in the east lane of Campground Road when they were struck by a 2004 Dodge pickup. They were taken to Spartanburg Regional Medical Center, where they later died from their injuries. The Spartanburg County Coroner's Office identified the bike rider as 57-year-old Geoffrey Berus of Wellford. The pickup driver was not injured. This is a developing story. items.t: SC woman disputes nearly $10K Duke Energy bill, says she’s relied on generator for over a year
items.x: NICHOLS, S.C. (WBTW) A South Carolina woman says she has been relying on a generator for more than a year after receiving a Duke Energy bill for nearly $10,000 that she disputes. items.x: ( NewsNation ) — As many as 75% of NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023 may have had chronic traumatic encephalopathy , better known as CTE, a new study from researchers at Boston University estimates. CTE is a "progressive neurodegenerative disease associated with exposure to repetitive head impacts, such as those from contact sport participation, military combat exposure, intimate partner violence, and other sources," according to the study. It is most frequently diagnosed in American football players. Researchers can identify the disease only after death, usually by examining donated brains. As a result, determining how many NFL players may have CTE has proven difficult. Most donations come from families whose loved ones had memory and behavior problems, two symptoms of the ailment, thus skewing results. items.t: Federal Reserve’s preferred measure of inflation rose slightly in September
items.x: ( The Hill ) Inflation increased slightly in September after declining in August , new data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis showed Thursday. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index , the preferred inflation metric for the Federal Reserve, rose by 0.5 percent last month and was up 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland projected PCE inflation for last month at 0.5 percent month-over-month and 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. Annual inflation, according to the PCE, previously dipped from 3.7 percent in July to 3.4 percent in August. The price of gas and other energy goods rose by 9.2 percent from August to September, after increasing by 4.4 percent from July to August. items.t: Salem restaurant to close after 30 years
items.x: SALEM, Ohio (WKBN) It's been an emotional day for a local family as it opened its doors to the community for one last time. Friday marked the final day of operations for Adele's Place in Salem, as owner Adele Lake is riding off into retirement. She's been working at the restaurant for over 50 years and has been the owner for the last 30. They have their regular customers, who spoke about how they've watched the family grow over the years. Many filed in on their final day for one last meal. "If you could have been here all this week, you couldn't get in the door. The parking lot was packed," Lake said. "The bread man couldn't even deliver his bread. He had to drop it off and leave. That's how busy we were. They have supported 100% since the day I opened." Lake says she's not sure what she will do with her time now, but says she will figure it out.

Shapiro was joined by State Senator James Malone (D), who flipped a red seat during a 2025 special election. The governor believes Malone's seat and five other State Senate seats are in play this year, but is optimistic Tuesday night "will be a good night" for Democrats. "I'm optimistic about all these races," Shapiro told reporters. "I think it's important to note that all those State Senate districts are really, really gerrymandered. It's really tough." Going into Election Day, Republicans hold a 27-23 seat majority in the Senate while Democrats have a 103-101 majority in the State House. items.t: Mercer County veterans honored at appreciation breakfast
items.x: HERMITAGE, Pa. (WKBN) An appreciation breakfast was held Friday morning in Mercer County at the VFW Hall. The event was started by Pennsylvania State Representative Parke Wentling to honor those who served and are currently serving our country. Pennsylvania Congressman Mike Kelly says the event has gone beyond anything he and Wentling ever imagined. "You feel it in the room. This is not a political event, which is really nice for a change to just go to something. We are honoring those who served and have put their lives on the line, the true 1% of American citizens," Kelly said. "To have an event like this and see all these veterans show up, it is so gratifying to be able to thank them for everything they've done." Kelly added that events like these help remind everyone that it is our veterans that made things safe for everyone and that it was an honor to spend the morning with them.

items.x: YOUNGSTOWN, Ohio (WKBN) The Butler Institute of American Art in downtown Youngstown is welcoming a new exhibit called "Michael Zagaris: 60 Years of NFL Photography." Over the course of his remarkable career, Zagaris has photographed 44 Super Bowls, 12 World Series and 14 MLB All-Star Games. His images capture several emotions such as concentration, vulnerability, celebration and defeat, forming an extraordinary visual record of American life and pop culture. An opening reception will be held at the Butler on Sunday from 1-3 p.m. It's free and open to the public. The exhibit will remain on display through April 25, 2027.

items.t: Turn this on to stop hackers from stealing your phone number
items.x: ( KTLA ) – Your phone number is more valuable than you might think. It doesn’t just let people call or text you. It can also be the key to getting into your bank accounts, email and other important services. That’s because so many companies still send two-factor authentication codes by text message. If a hacker takes control of your phone number, they could potentially intercept those codes and use them to break into your accounts, KTLA tech reporter Rich DeMuro explains. The attack is called SIM swapping. It happens when someone tricks your wireless carrier into transferring your phone number to a SIM card or eSIM they control. AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon all offer free security features designed to help prevent this. The catch? You typically have to turn them on yourself. Here’s exactly how to do it. items.t: Historic polar vortex disruption could influence Midwest weather late this year
items.x: ST. LOUIS Meteorologists are closely watching what could become one of the earliest major Sudden Stratospheric Warming (SSW) events on record. Forecast models are indicating a dramatic weakening, and possibly a temporary reversal of winds high above the Arctic during the first half of November. If the event occurs as predicted, it could disrupt the polar vortex weeks earlier than is typically observed during the northern hemisphere winter. What is a Sudden Stratospheric Warming? A Sudden Stratospheric Warming occurs when temperatures rapidly increase in the stratosphere, roughly 20 to 30 miles above the Earth's surface. This warming can weaken or even split the polar vortex the ring of strong winds that normally helps contain Arctic air near the North Pole. items.t: Up to 75% of NFL players who died had signs of CTE, new study says
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — As many as 75% of NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023 may have had chronic traumatic encephalopathy , better known as CTE, a new study from researchers at Boston University estimates. CTE is a "progressive neurodegenerative disease associated with exposure to repetitive head impacts, such as those from contact sport participation, military combat exposure, intimate partner violence, and other sources," according to the study. It is most frequently diagnosed in American football players. Researchers can identify the disease only after death, usually by examining donated brains. As a result, determining how many NFL players may have CTE has proven difficult. Most donations come from families whose loved ones had memory and behavior problems, two symptoms of the ailment, thus skewing results. LOUIS Prediction-market operator Kalshi has sued Missouri Attorney General Catherine Hanaway, seeking to block the state from enforcing sports betting laws against its sports prediction marketplace. Last month, Hanaway issued cease-and-desist letters to six prediction market operators , including Kalshi. She says they are operating as unlicensed sports wagering platforms in Missouri. In a new federal lawsuit, filed Tuesday, Kalshi asserts that it offers sports-event contracts that are federally-regulated financial products and therefore should not be subject to Missouri's sports betting laws. Missouri sports wagering framework, which took effect last December, imposes a 10% wagering tax and mandates that online platforms actively prevent wager by individuals under 21. items.t: New app turns Congress into a fantasy sports competition
items.x: AUSTIN (Nexstar) — On Tuesday night, Texans will select 35 members of Congress to represent them for the next two years. Soon after, they can add those lawmakers to fantasy teams and track how well they govern once they're in Washington. Inspired by his love of fantasy football, Houstonian-turned-Austinite Alex Kurkowski created the app RabbleRouser this year using the AI-powered tool Claude. The app allows users to draft U.S. senators and representatives who rack up points by introducing legislation, taking votes and advancing bills through Congress. "During the (NFL) offseason, there's nothing going on. So I figured, Hey, why not get into politics?'" Kurkowski said. "So I just built it starting from scratch just because of the void of fantasy football." items.t: Trump tariffs hitting small business owners in multiple ways
items.x: WASHINGTON, D.C. (NEXSTAR) President Trump says his tariffs are helping the American economy grow but for some small businesses, the math isn't working out. From higher prices to fewer products on store shelves, one Virginia shop is finding ways to adapt. For Ben Knezic, running The Cut Butchery in Alexandria, Virginia – a Washington suburb – means offering customers a little bit of everything. From fresh meats and seafood to imported wines, cheeses and specialty foods, Knezic says Trump's tariffs are making some of those products more expensive. “Just seeing prices on our goods go up and up,” said Knezic. “We've had to raise prices on a lot of things like cheese and wine and some of the other stuff we import."
