items.t: Nocturnal neighbors: Austin Bat Refuge busts common misconceptions
items.x: AUSTIN (KXAN) Millions of bats live alongside us in Central Texas. One group of experts works to rehabilitate creatures that need care and educate people about how to live alongside these nocturnal neighbors. Ahead of Halloween, Hilary Pelham with the refuge explained some of the common misconceptions about these animals. For example, none of the 10 species that live in the Austin area drink blood but rather are insectivores. "I like to say that the scariest thing about bats is what would happen if we didn't have them," she said. "That would mean agricultural collapse." She said that Mexican Free-Tailed bats, famous for emerging from under the Congress Avenue Bridge every night, eat crop pests saving billions of dollars in agricultural costs per year for farmers. items.t: Healthcare becomes key midterm issue ahead of policy changes
items.x: (DC BUREAU) – Healthcare costs could rise for insured Americans as states prepare to enforce new Medicaid restrictions in January under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act. The legislation, signed by President Donald Trump, requires states to enforce stricter Medicaid work requirements and mandate that enrollees reapply twice a year. The nonpartisan Congressional Budget Office projects millions of Americans will lose healthcare coverage as a result of the changes. Policy analysts warn the loss of coverage will impact hospital systems. Round Rock (6-3, 3-2), meanwhile, saw its district championship hopes take a hit with the loss. items.t: Bell County voter’s mail-in ballot not delivered; USPS says issue is isolated
items.x: KILLEEN, TX (KXAN) With early voting underway and the midterm election just days away, KXAN has received emails and calls from viewers asking for help looking into issues they dealt with when trying to cast their votes. Robert Anderson, of Killeen, sent in a photo of his wife's ballot which he said the U.S. Post Office rejected. He told KXAN he mailed the ballot on Thursday. It showed up in his mailbox on Saturday with a bright yellow "Return to Sender" sticker. A Bell County woman's mail-in ballot was returned with "Return to Sender" stamped on it. (Courtesy Robert Anderson) "How can that be? I mean, it's the same address that it's been for years. The same post office box in Belton. How can somebody not know what it is?" Anderson questioned. "Unless this was totally automated and it was kicked out by an automated machine that had an error. I don't know." KXAN reached out to Bell County.

items.x: AUSTIN (KXAN) A newly-released recording of a September federal court hearing reveals audio of the traffic stop that led to a pursuit and ended in an ICE agent shooting a Venezuelan man last month. The recording, first reported by KUT and now obtained by KXAN, captured the preliminary and detention hearings for Wilber Garces Perez. The United States Attorney's Office for the Western District of Texas charged Garces Perez with assaulting, resisting and impeding a federal officer for his actions prior to being shot in north Austin on Sept. 20. During the hearings held on Sept. 30, Homeland Security Investigations Special Agent Rick Bazan detailed his investigation. He referred to the two ICE agents, who serve as Enforcement Removal Operations (ERO) officers, by their initials throughout the hearing DF and LG. items.t: VIDEO: Driver hits Texas deputy’s car while at DWI stop
items.x: CONROE, Texas (CW39) A passing driver struck a patrol car's door and injured a Montgomery County deputy as he was getting out, according to the sheriff's office. The crash happened early Saturday morning while the deputy was helping with a suspected DWI stop on Interstate 45. The sheriff's office said the passing driver failed to move over or slow down before hitting the door. The deputy was taken to a hospital, and the 33-year-old woman driving the car was arrested and charged with DWI, passing an emergency vehicle causing bodily injury and failure to stop and render aid. The driver in the original stop was also arrested for DWI. Both drivers were booked in the Montgomery County Jail.

items.t: Potential Binance ‘hack’ forces crypto firms to freeze $3 billion
items.x: ( The Hill ) A suspected hack at Binance prompted cryptocurrency firms to freeze about $3 billion in assets, the company said on Thursday. The exchange, which described the situation as a "security issue," has temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals while it "conducts security checks, freezes funds, and works with law enforcement." It vowed to cover all losses. "It does look like a hack on Binance," the company's co-founder Changpeng Zhao wrote in a post on the social platform X. He touted fellow crypto firms Tether and Circle for quickly freezing funds. Zhao acknowledged he no longer manages the company but said he expects "all user funds will be fully covered." The Binance co-founder stepped down as CEO in 2023 when he pleaded guilty to violating anti-money laundering laws. President Trump pardoned Zhao in November 2025. APD expects an estimated 80,000 to 100,000 people to descend upon the city's entertainment district, which includes Rainey Street, East Sixth Street and West Sixth Street. items.t: Inside the Torchy’s Tacos turnaround plan after store closures
items.x: AUSTIN (ABJ) — Torchy’s Tacos closed seven locations earlier this year. Shedding those stores was part of the company’s new growth plan. The Austin-based taco chain is sitting at about 120 locations and has new restaurants in the pipeline. But previously, Torchy’s Tacos grew into too many new markets at once and it opened stores that weren’t the right size, CEO Paul Macaluso said. The company closed restaurants that were losing money, causing a large drain on the business and preventing it from growing the right way, the CEO told the ABJ. The company closed seven stores in August 2025 and seven more in February 2026. Since February, Torchy’s Tacos has opened multiple locations. items.t: Federal Reserve’s preferred measure of inflation rose slightly in September
items.x: ( The Hill ) Inflation increased slightly in September after declining in August , new data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis showed Thursday. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index , the preferred inflation metric for the Federal Reserve, rose by 0.5 percent last month and was up 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland projected PCE inflation for last month at 0.5 percent month-over-month and 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. Annual inflation, according to the PCE, previously dipped from 3.7 percent in July to 3.4 percent in August. The price of gas and other energy goods rose by 9.2 percent from August to September, after increasing by 4.4 percent from July to August. items.t: AUDIO: Hear the initial interaction between ICE agents and the man shot in north Austin
items.x: AUSTIN (KXAN) A newly-released recording of a September federal court hearing reveals audio of the traffic stop that led to a pursuit and ended in an ICE agent shooting a Venezuelan man last month. The recording, first reported by KUT and now obtained by KXAN, captured the preliminary and detention hearings for Wilber Garces Perez. The United States Attorney's Office for the Western District of Texas charged Garces Perez with assaulting, resisting and impeding a federal officer for his actions prior to being shot in north Austin on Sept. 20. During the hearings held on Sept. 30, Homeland Security Investigations Special Agent Rick Bazan detailed his investigation. He referred to the two ICE agents, who serve as Enforcement Removal Operations (ERO) officers, by their initials throughout the hearing DF and LG. items.t: VIDEO: Driver hits Texas deputy’s car while at DWI stop
items.x: CONROE, Texas (CW39) A passing driver struck a patrol car's door and injured a Montgomery County deputy as he was getting out, according to the sheriff's office. The crash happened early Saturday morning while the deputy was helping with a suspected DWI stop on Interstate 45. The sheriff's office said the passing driver failed to move over or slow down before hitting the door. The deputy was taken to a hospital, and the 33-year-old woman driving the car was arrested and charged with DWI, passing an emergency vehicle causing bodily injury and failure to stop and render aid. The driver in the original stop was also arrested for DWI. Both drivers were booked in the Montgomery County Jail.

items.t: Potential Binance ‘hack’ forces crypto firms to freeze $3 billion
items.x: ( The Hill ) A suspected hack at Binance prompted cryptocurrency firms to freeze about $3 billion in assets, the company said on Thursday. The exchange, which described the situation as a "security issue," has temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals while it "conducts security checks, freezes funds, and works with law enforcement." It vowed to cover all losses. "It does look like a hack on Binance," the company's co-founder Changpeng Zhao wrote in a post on the social platform X. He touted fellow crypto firms Tether and Circle for quickly freezing funds. Zhao acknowledged he no longer manages the company but said he expects "all user funds will be fully covered." The Binance co-founder stepped down as CEO in 2023 when he pleaded guilty to violating anti-money laundering laws. President Trump pardoned Zhao in November 2025. items.t: Travis County Expo Center site considered for NHL expansion

items.t: Austin stocks over 7,000 grass carp in Lake Austin to fight hydrilla
items.x: AUSTIN (KXAN) — Austin Watershed Protection released 7,091 sterile grass carp into Lake Austin as part of an ongoing effort to control hydrilla, an invasive aquatic plant that can clog waterways and interfere with recreation. Hydrilla growth in Lake Austin plateaus The fish were stocked Thursday near Jessica Hollis Park, the Walsh Boat Ramp and Bull Creek areas where hydrilla growth has been most concentrated, according to AWP. Grass carp are used as a biological management tool because they prefer eating hydrilla over many native aquatic plants. City officials said the goal is to reduce dense hydrilla growth while maintaining enough vegetation to support a healthy lake. According to a September survey conducted by Texas Parks and Wildlife, Lake Austin contained an estimated 575 acres of hydrilla. items.t: Bicyclist killed in east Austin crash
items.x: AUSTIN (KXAN) —Police are investigating a fatal crash involving a vehicle and a bicyclist Thursday evening in east Austin. MAP: Where have Austin’s fatal crashes occurred in 2026? According to the Austin Police Department, officers responded to a traffic fatality call that came in at about 6:51 p.m. in the 8100 block of Loyola Lane near Decker Lane. First responders performed CPR on the adult bicycle rider but efforts were unsuccessful. APD said in an update that the driver of the vehicle stayed on scene and is cooperating with the investigation. The incident is being investigated as Austin’s 72nd fatal crash of 2026, resulting in 74 deaths, according to APD. On the date of this crash in 2025, 80 fatal crashes resulted in 84 deaths. Campaigns, political parties, and partisan and non-partisan organizations have tried inspiring people to vote through messages, mailers, and TV ads. For example, on Thursday one organization sent Texas voters a video of rapper Ice-T reminding and encouraging people to vote on election day this upcoming Tuesday. But a new GOTV tool implemented by Gov. Greg Abbott's campaign last year is tapping into the personal networks of Texas voters. Abbott Impact On Tuesday, at a campaign stop in Harlingen, Abbott told a crowd of supporters to pull their phones out, directed them to the App Store, and asked them to download the Abbott Impact app. His campaign launched the app last October. The Jaguars (4-5, 3-2) have found their offensive rhythm after dropping their first two district games, outscoring opponents 200-13 over their past three contests. Thursday's win strengthens Buda Johnson's playoff positioning heading into the final week of the regular season. Austin High (3-6, 3-3), meanwhile, closes its regular season with a loss after turning things around in district play. All three of the Maroons' victories came against district opponents, including two shutout wins. Buda Johnson wraps up its regular season in Week 11 against Bowie, which entered Thursday's action second in the district standings. Catch more Texas high school football live on KXAN+ this season. items.t: UT dedicates Architecture & Planning Library to Texas’ first Black licensed architect John S. Chase
items.x: AUSTIN (KXAN) The University of Texas at Austin celebrated the dedication of the John S. Chase Architecture and Planning Library last week in a ceremony naming the building after the UT alum, who was Texas' first Black licensed architect. Chase enrolled at the university just two days after the Supreme Court's 1950 ruling in Sweatt v. Painter that challenged segregation in higher education, according to a release from UT. He earned a Master of Architecture in 1952 and built a career designing "bright, minimalistic spaces that were community centered," according to UT. The university held a dedication celebration on Oct. 22, with state, local, and university leaders in attendance, including UT President Jim Davis, Regent Jodie Jiles, Provost William Inboden, Senior Vice Provost and UT Libraries Director Robert H. items.t: Pickup truck driver killed in crash with commercial vehicle in Travis County
items.x: AUSTIN (KXAN) — The Texas Department of Public Safety is investigating a fatal two-vehicle crash on FM 2322, also known as Pace Bend Road, in western Travis County. According to DPS, the crash occurred in the 1900 block of FM 2322 and involved a commercial motor vehicle and a pickup truck. DPS said the driver of the pickup truck died at the scene. Journalism student Desirae Gutierrez decided to dig into the issue after hearing teachers and students talking about the topic. "There is definitely less one-on-one time with the teachers," said Gutierrez. "Since I knew about there being a lot of budget cuts, I was hearing about how teachers have more students." The Austin Independent School District said due to staff leveling after the finalization of the 2026-27 budget, most class sizes, across all departments, are larger than they have been in years before. items.x: AUSTIN (KXAN) Austin Police are preparing for large crowds ahead of a busy Halloween weekend in downtown Austin. APD expects an estimated 80,000 to 100,000 people to descend upon the city's entertainment district, which includes Rainey Street, East Sixth Street and West Sixth Street. An already popular weekend in Austin is expected to get even busier. Not only does Halloween fall on a Saturday this year, but Sunday morning marks the end of daylight saving time. items.t: How dangerous are construction zones?
items.x: Bastrop County, TX (KXAN) Two construction workers died early Thursday morning while working on a project in Bastrop County after a vehicle crashed into the work zone on State Highway 71 near Tucker Hill Lane. This is the first time since December 2021 that a construction worker was killed in a work zone in the TxDOT Austin District. That crash, which occurred in southeast Austin, also killed two workers. Work zone safety campaigns are a part of the Texas Department of Transportation's awareness efforts for drivers, particularly because the vast majority of work zone crashes injure drivers or their passengers—not the workers. items.t: Inside the Torchy’s Tacos turnaround plan after store closures
items.x: AUSTIN (ABJ) — Torchy’s Tacos closed seven locations earlier this year. Shedding those stores was part of the company’s new growth plan. The Austin-based taco chain is sitting at about 120 locations and has new restaurants in the pipeline. But previously, Torchy’s Tacos grew into too many new markets at once and it opened stores that weren’t the right size, CEO Paul Macaluso said. The company closed restaurants that were losing money, causing a large drain on the business and preventing it from growing the right way, the CEO told the ABJ. The company closed seven stores in August 2025 and seven more in February 2026. Since February, Torchy’s Tacos has opened multiple locations. Read the rest of this story in the Austin Business Journal .

He answered “no” to each charge as his lawyer, Ian Winter, asked whether he was guilty of three counts of rape, three counts of sexual assault and one count of attempted indecent assault. items.t: Federal Reserve’s preferred measure of inflation rose slightly in September
items.x: ( The Hill ) Inflation increased slightly in September after declining in August , new data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis showed Thursday. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index , the preferred inflation metric for the Federal Reserve, rose by 0.5 percent last month and was up 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland projected PCE inflation for last month at 0.5 percent month-over-month and 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. Annual inflation, according to the PCE, previously dipped from 3.7 percent in July to 3.4 percent in August. The price of gas and other energy goods rose by 9.2 percent from August to September, after increasing by 4.4 percent from July to August. items.x: ( The Hill ) The Trump administration's bid to separate 20,000 mail ballots in California that it says are likely noncitizens met another defeat on Wednesday as a trial judge refused to intervene. He was 92. Nominated by then-President Bill Clinton in 1998, Hellerstein oversaw many high-profile disputes during his nearly three decades on the bench in New York City. items.x: EL PASO, Texas (Border Report) An off-duty U.S. Border Patrol agent allegedly stabbed and killed his wife early Wednesday morning in Laredo, Texas, according to the Laredo Morning Times. The newspaper reported that Abel Garza, 30, is charged with murder in the death of his wife, 28-year-old Mayra Alejandra Landeros. The newspaper also reported that U.S. Customs and Border Protection confirmed that Garza is a U.S. Border Patrol agent with the Laredo Sector, and that the agency’s Office of Professional Responsibility is reviewing the incident.

items.t: 3 killed in SH 71 construction zone crash, including 2 contractors
items.x: BASTROP COUNTY, Texas (KXAN) — Three people were killed, including two contractors, following a crash on State Highway 71 near Tucker Hill Lane that occurred in a construction zone early Thursday morning. items.t: Turn this on to stop hackers from stealing your phone number
items.x: ( KTLA ) – Your phone number is more valuable than you might think. It doesn’t just let people call or text you. It can also be the key to getting into your bank accounts, email and other important services. That’s because so many companies still send two-factor authentication codes by text message. If a hacker takes control of your phone number, they could potentially intercept those codes and use them to break into your accounts, KTLA tech reporter Rich DeMuro explains. The attack is called SIM swapping. It happens when someone tricks your wireless carrier into transferring your phone number to a SIM card or eSIM they control. AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon all offer free security features designed to help prevent this. The catch? You typically have to turn them on yourself. Here’s exactly how to do it. items.t: Space heaters sold at Costco nationwide are recalled over fire hazards
items.x: NEW YORK ( WPIX ) Thousands of space heaters are being recalled after more than a dozen reports of units catching fire, according to the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. About 338,800 DREO space heaters were sold from September 2025 to October 2026 at Costco stores nationwide and online by retailers including Costco, Best Buy, Kohl's, Lowes, QVC and Home Depot. items.t: Up to 75% of NFL players who died had signs of CTE, new study says
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — As many as 75% of NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023 may have had chronic traumatic encephalopathy , better known as CTE, a new study from researchers at Boston University estimates. CTE is a "progressive neurodegenerative disease associated with exposure to repetitive head impacts, such as those from contact sport participation, military combat exposure, intimate partner violence, and other sources," according to the study. It is most frequently diagnosed in American football players. Researchers can identify the disease only after death, usually by examining donated brains. As a result, determining how many NFL players may have CTE has proven difficult. Most donations come from families whose loved ones had memory and behavior problems, two symptoms of the ailment, thus skewing results. items.t: Death of ‘Mad Max’ actor Richard Norton linked to peptides, coroner says
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — The death of Australian actor Richard Norton has been linked to injecting unapproved peptides , according to a new coroner's report. Norton, 75, went into cardiac arrest in March 2025 after injecting prescribed but unapproved CJC1295 and ipamorelin, according to multiple reports . "Richard's death was triggered by his injection of the peptide CJC1295/Ipamorelin," the report reads. "Richard had been taking amounts of the medication in excess of the dose prescribed by his medical practitioner. The injection caused an anaphylactic reaction which in turn led to cardiac arrest." Norton was known for his role in "Mad Max: Fury Road," "The Octagon," and more, as well as his martial arts scenes with heavyweights of the genre, such as Jackie Chan and Chuck Norris. The majority comprised U.S. Circuit Judge Gabriel Sanchez, an appointee of former President Biden, and U.S. Circuit Judge Mark Bennett, appointed by President Trump. items.t: Turn this on to stop hackers from stealing your phone number
items.x: ( KTLA ) – Your phone number is more valuable than you might think. It doesn’t just let people call or text you. It can also be the key to getting into your bank accounts, email and other important services. That’s because so many companies still send two-factor authentication codes by text message. If a hacker takes control of your phone number, they could potentially intercept those codes and use them to break into your accounts, KTLA tech reporter Rich DeMuro explains. The attack is called SIM swapping. It happens when someone tricks your wireless carrier into transferring your phone number to a SIM card or eSIM they control. AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon all offer free security features designed to help prevent this. The catch? You typically have to turn them on yourself. Here’s exactly how to do it. items.t: Miami Twp. man indicted for murder of 10-year-old daughter
items.x: A Miami Township man has been indicted for the murder of his 10-year-old daughter. Scott Cleaver, 48, was arrested on Thursday by the Southern Ohio Fugitive Apprehension Strike Team. he was indicted later that day by the Montgomery County Grand Jury. His arrest follows a yearlong investigation by Miami Township Police Department that began after a call to a home on 10421 Aldora Drive on Oct. 1, 2025. 10-year-old Rylie was found dead. Cleaver faces three charges including Involuntary Manslaughter (F1), Reckless Homicide (F3) and Endangering Children (F3). This case remains under investigation.

items.t: Up to 75% of NFL players who died had signs of CTE, new study says
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — As many as 75% of NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023 may have had chronic traumatic encephalopathy , better known as CTE, a new study from researchers at Boston University estimates. CTE is a "progressive neurodegenerative disease associated with exposure to repetitive head impacts, such as those from contact sport participation, military combat exposure, intimate partner violence, and other sources," according to the study. It is most frequently diagnosed in American football players. Researchers can identify the disease only after death, usually by examining donated brains. As a result, determining how many NFL players may have CTE has proven difficult. Most donations come from families whose loved ones had memory and behavior problems, two symptoms of the ailment, thus skewing results. items.t: GM settles $220M lawsuit for allegedly selling private driver data
items.x: HARTFORD, Conn. ( WTNH ) — General Motors has agreed to pay $220 million to settle claims that it illegally sold drivers' private data and location information to third parties. The settlement, announced Thursday, concerns allegations that GM had sold the information to data brokers, who in turn sold it to insurance companies. That private data, in part, was then used to set insurance rates, according to a coalition of attorneys general in 35 states and Washington D.C. “GM turned private vehicles into mobile insurance surveillance machines without consumer consent or awareness," Connecticut Attorney General William Tong said in a Thursday press release announcing the settlement. "GM profited from the sale of this personal driving data, and consumers paid the price in the form of higher premiums." items.t: Ohio receives over $8M from General Motors settlement
items.x: DAYTON, Ohio ( WDTN ) – Ohio will receive over $8 million following a settlement with General Motors over allegations that it illegally sold consumers’ driving behavior and location data to third parties. From 2016 to 2024, GM enrolled millions of drivers in its Smart Driver program, which tracks driving habits. The company told drivers that it wouldn’t share their data with insurers without their consent. However, GM later sold the data to insurance brokers, who then passed it to insurance companies to adjust premiums based on driving habits. This data sale was not disclosed to customers. “GM broke consumers’ trust by selling such data without their knowledge and consent,” said Ohio Attorney General Andy Wilson. “Ohioans should not have to worry that the information collected by their own vehicles will be used against them. Peltz’s Trian Fund Management and several partners are offering Wendy’s $7.35 per share in cash, or a premium of nearly 19% over the stock’s closing price on Tuesday, in a deal that would take the company private. The offer values Wendy's at $1.4 billion. Wendy's, which is based in Dublin, Ohio, confirmed receipt of the unsolicited proposal in a statement Wednesday and said its board has formed an independent committee to evaluate it. At the end of last year, Wendy's had 5,969 restaurants in the U.S. and 1,428 outlets in 38 countries. If your child has allergies, Middleton recommends carrying an EpiPen or another allergy medicine just in case. She says parents should have a way to identify their kids in a crowd when wearing costumes. "Make sure that costumes are well-fitting. items.t: Turn this on to stop hackers from stealing your phone number
items.x: ( KTLA ) – Your phone number is more valuable than you might think. It doesn’t just let people call or text you. It can also be the key to getting into your bank accounts, email and other important services. That’s because so many companies still send two-factor authentication codes by text message. If a hacker takes control of your phone number, they could potentially intercept those codes and use them to break into your accounts, KTLA tech reporter Rich DeMuro explains. The attack is called SIM swapping. It happens when someone tricks your wireless carrier into transferring your phone number to a SIM card or eSIM they control. AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon all offer free security features designed to help prevent this. The catch? You typically have to turn them on yourself. Here’s exactly how to do it. items.t: Christa Pike says she remains in constant pain after botched execution in Tennessee
items.x: NASHVILLE, Tenn. ( WKRN ) — A month after Tennessee failed to execute the only woman on death row, Christa Pike has released a statement through her attorneys. Pike, 50, said she had been "prepared to die" when she entered the execution chamber at a Tennessee prison last month. Then, after surviving the failed execution by lethal injection, she said she "woke up alone in a hospital confused and in pain." "There hasn’t been a moment since that night when I haven’t been in pain. My body hurts. My arms hurt," Pike said in the statement. "My hands hurt. My throat hurts. I still struggle to speak. And the pain isn’t just physical. There is pain in my mind and in my soul." Doctors on Pike's legal team suggest the IV line was not placed properly, causing the lethal injection drugs to enter surrounding tissue rather than her bloodstream. items.x: MEMPHIS, Tenn. The search for escaped convicted murderer Jacob Morley remains a top priority for law enforcement agencies across the country, and for the family of the man he was convicted of killing, every day he remains free is another day of uncertainty and fear. Morley, 28, escaped Sunday night from the Northwest Correctional Complex in Tiptonville while serving a life sentence for the 2022 murder of Cody Birchfield. Jacob Morley, TBI Authorities say he breached the prison's perimeter fence before stealing a white Ford F-350 that was later recovered in Marion, Illinois. Despite an expanding multi-state manhunt, Morley has not been found. The Tennessee Bureau of Investigation has placed Morley on its Most Wanted list, and authorities continue urging the public not to approach him if spotted. items.t: Leo XIV becomes first pope ever to vote in US general election
items.x: VATICAN CITY (AP) — Pope Leo XIV has become the first pope to vote in a U.S. general election. The Vatican confirmed Friday that the Chicago-born pontiff had submitted a mail-in ballot in Chicago ahead of November’s midterm elections, citing his long-standing belief in civic participation. Leo, formerly Robert Prevost, “has exercised his right to vote as a United States citizen” and has done so “whenever he was eligible to do so,” the Holy See press office said. The statement said he had also voted while living in Peru whenever he was eligible. “The Holy Father expresses his belief in the right and the duty of citizens to participate in democratic processes,” it added. Leo’s vote was first reported by the Chicago Sun-Times, which quoted the chief of staff at the Will County clerk’s office as saying the pope, registered at a New Lenox address, requested a mail-in ballot on Oct. 3. The exchange, which described the situation as a "security issue," has temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals while it "conducts security checks, freezes funds, and works with law enforcement." It vowed to cover all losses. "It does look like a hack on Binance," the company's co-founder Changpeng Zhao wrote in a post on the social platform X. He touted fellow crypto firms Tether and Circle for quickly freezing funds. Zhao acknowledged he no longer manages the company but said he expects "all user funds will be fully covered." The Binance co-founder stepped down as CEO in 2023 when he pleaded guilty to violating anti-money laundering laws. President Trump pardoned Zhao in November 2025. items.t: Texas says 9 islands in Rio Grande belong to state, not Mexico
items.x: HARLINGEN, Texas ( Border Report ) The State of Texas on Tuesday declared that nine river islands in the middle of the Rio Grande belong to the state, not to Mexico. For years, river islands have provided what officials says are safe havens for cartels that smuggle drugs and migrants into the U.S. from Mexico, giving them a place to hide and wait out border patrols in those areas. A couple years ago, however, the Texas General Land Office declared some islands a part of the state and cleared them of vegetation. Some islands have had military troops land on them recently, and some are also used as border security staging zones. items.t: Evidence suppression request withdrawn in Jackson County murder case
items.x: SCOTTSBORO, Ala. (WHNT) — Lawyers for a woman accused in the murder of Jamari Moore moved to withdraw their motion to suppress evidence. Circuit Court judge John Graham granted that motion on Tuesday. In August, lawyers for Johneil Steadman filed a motion to suppress "circumstantial and conflicting evidence" obtained by the Jackson County Sheriff's Office. A hearing was set for Tuesday to argue that motion, but the defense instead withdrew it. Investigators allege Steadman and her partner, Tapanga Steadman, were involved in the killing of Moore, whose body was found wrapped in plastic and floating in the Sauty Creek near Lake Guntersville. Johneil Steadman was arrested on Christmas Day in 2025. Both have been held without bond under an Aniah's Law ruling .

items.t: GM settles $220M lawsuit for allegedly selling private driver data

items.t: Federal Reserve’s preferred measure of inflation rose slightly in September

The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index , the preferred inflation metric for the Federal Reserve, rose by 0.5 percent last month and was up 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland projected PCE inflation for last month at 0.5 percent month-over-month and 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. Annual inflation, according to the PCE, previously dipped from 3.7 percent in July to 3.4 percent in August. The price of gas and other energy goods rose by 9.2 percent from August to September, after increasing by 4.4 percent from July to August. items.t: Turn this on to stop hackers from stealing your phone number
items.x: ( KTLA ) – Your phone number is more valuable than you might think. It doesn’t just let people call or text you. It can also be the key to getting into your bank accounts, email and other important services. That’s because so many companies still send two-factor authentication codes by text message. If a hacker takes control of your phone number, they could potentially intercept those codes and use them to break into your accounts, KTLA tech reporter Rich DeMuro explains. The attack is called SIM swapping. It happens when someone tricks your wireless carrier into transferring your phone number to a SIM card or eSIM they control. AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon all offer free security features designed to help prevent this. The catch? You typically have to turn them on yourself. Here’s exactly how to do it. items.t: Man handed maximum sentence for role in girlfriend’s murder in Fort Wayne
items.x: FORT WAYNE, Ind. (WANE) A man convicted of murder in the death of his girlfriend was handed the maximum sentence Friday. A judge in Allen Superior Court sentenced 55-year-old Reginald Brooks to 65 years in prison for murder, with 20 more years tacked on for a gun enhancement. A jury previously found Brooks guilty in the murder of Sajdah Abdur-Rabb. The 50-year-old woman was found dead in January 2025 at a mobile home on Dunkelberg Road, near the corner of Bluffton Road and Airport Expressway. Investigators determined Brooks shot her during a drunken fight after allegedly threatening to kill her and her child.

The murder charge carried a maximum sentence of 65 years, but a jury also determined that the guilty verdict included the enhancement, tacking on an additional 20 years to his sentence. Kizer Jr. was accused and found guilty of shooting and killing 20-year-old Jathen Maxwell in July of 2024 . Afterward, he allegedly posted the words "head shot" on social media, along with videos of him rapping with lyrics referencing the murder. items.t: DOJ sentences Wabash man for possessing over 2,000 images of CSAM
items.x: WABASH COUNTY, Ind. (WANE) A man from Wabash, Indiana, has been sentenced to over six years in prison by the Department of Justice for possession of child sex abuse material (CSAM). Friday, the DOJ sentenced 31-year-old Cody Smith to 80 months in prison, or just over six years and six months, followed by another seven years of supervised release. He was also ordered to pay $18,000 in restitution to the victims. Smith was arrested after agents with the Department of Homeland Security executed a search warrant at his home in Wabash. There, the agents recovered his cell phone, which contained over 2,000 images and videos of CSAM. Data from his phone also showed Smith sharing preferences and the collection with others. Smith pleaded guilty to his crime.

items.t: 1 dead, 1 hurt in fire that displaced residents at Albion apartment complex
items.x: ALBION, Ind. (WANE) One person died and another was seriously hurt during a blaze Thursday at an apartment complex in Albion. Firefighters responded just after 9:30 p.m. to one of the buildings on Autumn Hills Drive, according to a Facebook post from the Albion Volunteer Fire Department. One of the residents died. Another was seriously injured while trying to alert neighbors about the fire, the department said. That person had to be flown to a Fort Wayne hospital for treatment. The victims have not been identified. The fire displaced multiple other residents who are being aided by local charities, the department said. The cause of the fire has not been revealed. The investigation is being led by the Indiana State Fire Marshal's Office. "They will not release their findings for a few weeks," the social media post explained. items.t: Fort Wayne man sentenced for mishandling gun, fatally shooting niece
items.x: FORT WAYNE, Ind. (WANE) A man was sentenced Friday for shooting a family member in 2024 after mishandling a gun. A judge in Allen Superior Court handed Davion Vaughn Foster three years in prison for his role in the death of Myuanna Foster-Juarez, his teenage niece. It happened in August 2024; her death was ruled a homicide. A witness told police at the scene that Foster said he'd accidentally dropped a gun while in Myuanna's room at a home on Winter Street. Foster, 27, pleaded guilty to reckless homicide this past August. The plea deal capped his sentence at three years.

"There hasn’t been a moment since that night when I haven’t been in pain. My body hurts. My arms hurt," Pike said in the statement. "My hands hurt. My throat hurts. I still struggle to speak. And the pain isn’t just physical. There is pain in my mind and in my soul." items.x: (WJW) Ground cinnamon is being recalled in 14 states just as seasonal baking gets underway. items.t: Up to 75% of NFL players who died had signs of CTE, new study says
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — As many as 75% of NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023 may have had chronic traumatic encephalopathy , better known as CTE, a new study from researchers at Boston University estimates. CTE is a "progressive neurodegenerative disease associated with exposure to repetitive head impacts, such as those from contact sport participation, military combat exposure, intimate partner violence, and other sources," according to the study. It is most frequently diagnosed in American football players. Researchers can identify the disease only after death, usually by examining donated brains. As a result, determining how many NFL players may have CTE has proven difficult. Most donations come from families whose loved ones had memory and behavior problems, two symptoms of the ailment, thus skewing results. It can also be the key to getting into your bank accounts, email and other important services. That’s because so many companies still send two-factor authentication codes by text message. And the pain isn’t just physical. There is pain in my mind and in my soul." items.t: Up to 75% of NFL players who died had signs of CTE, new study says
items.x: (NewsNation) — As many as 75% of NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023 may have had chronic traumatic encephalopathy, better known as CTE, a new study from researchers at Boston University estimates. CTE is a "progressive neurodegenerative disease associated with exposure to repetitive head impacts, such as those from contact sport participation, military combat exposure, intimate partner violence, and other sources," according to the study. It is most frequently diagnosed in American football players. Researchers can identify the disease only after death, usually by examining donated brains. As a result, determining how many NFL players may have CTE has proven difficult. Most donations come from families whose loved ones had memory and behavior problems, two symptoms of the ailment, thus skewing results. Here’s how Richmonders can recycle their pumpkins after Halloween
items.x: RICHMOND, Va. (WRIC) The jack-o'-lantern is a Halloween staple, but what do you do with those pumpkins once November arrives? Richmond officials are launching a new program that aims to keep them out of landfills. Starting on Sunday, Nov. 1, Richmond residents can recycle pumpkins at designated recycling centers through the city's new "Pumpkin Round-Up Program." Those facilities, located at 1710 Robin Hood Rd. and 7400 Forrest Hill Ave., will accept pumpkins through Monday, Nov. 30. According to the city, each year, many pumpkins are thrown away with everyday household waste and ultimately sent to a landfill. items.t: A historic drop for Alphabet’s stock drags the US market lower
items.x: NEW YORK (AP) — A historic drop for Alphabet’s stock dragged the U.S. market lower Thursday after the company behind Google and YouTube reported weaker growth for the summer than analysts expected. The report underscored worries about whether all its huge investments in artificial-intelligence technology will pay off. The S&P 500 fell 0.3% for its first loss in four days, even though the wide majority of stocks rose within the index and across Wall Street. The Nasdaq composite tumbled 1.4%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 132 points, or 0.3%. Alphabet is one of the most influential stocks on Wall Street because it’s one of the largest, and the Class A shares of its stock fell 12.6% for their worst day since they began trading more than 20 years ago. items.t: Virginia DWR celebrates Bat Week with cute stickers, more
items.x: RICHMOND, Va. (WRIC) Virginia's Department of Wildlife Resources (DWR) is celebrating Bat Week until Oct. 31 with a guide to Virginia's bats, stickers and more. The DWR took to Facebook earlier this week to highlight its collection of bat-themed merchandise, with donations set to support habitat restoration through the department's Restore the Wild program. According to the Virginia Department of Conservation and Recreation (DCR), Bat Week runs from Oct. 24 to 31 each year to celebrate bats, encourage conservation and highlight the role the animals play in ecosystems around the world. Virginia is home to 17 species of bats , according to the DWR. Of those, three species are considered Federally Endangered and one is listed as State Endangered. items.x: NEW CASTLE, Va. (WFXR) Expect to hear the thunder of gunfire around Virginia soon. Deer muzzleloader season opens October 31. But, before you head into the woods, there is one very important thing to consider. "Is my gun ready?" The only way to tell is to fire it at a target to make sure the scope and gun are in synch, and that your aim is true. If not, you will need to make adjustments on the scope and possibly the gun. There are any number of things that can affect the scope. items.t: Turn this on to stop hackers from stealing your phone number
items.x: ( KTLA ) – Your phone number is more valuable than you might think. It doesn’t just let people call or text you. It can also be the key to getting into your bank accounts, email and other important services. That’s because so many companies still send two-factor authentication codes by text message. If a hacker takes control of your phone number, they could potentially intercept those codes and use them to break into your accounts, KTLA tech reporter Rich DeMuro explains. The attack is called SIM swapping. It happens when someone tricks your wireless carrier into transferring your phone number to a SIM card or eSIM they control. AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon all offer free security features designed to help prevent this. The catch? You typically have to turn them on yourself. Here’s exactly how to do it. items.t: Death of ‘Mad Max’ actor Richard Norton linked to peptides, coroner says
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — The death of Australian actor Richard Norton has been linked to injecting unapproved peptides , according to a new coroner's report. Norton, 75, went into cardiac arrest in March 2025 after injecting prescribed but unapproved CJC1295 and ipamorelin, according to multiple reports . "Richard's death was triggered by his injection of the peptide CJC1295/Ipamorelin," the report reads. "Richard had been taking amounts of the medication in excess of the dose prescribed by his medical practitioner. The injection caused an anaphylactic reaction which in turn led to cardiac arrest." Norton was known for his role in "Mad Max: Fury Road," "The Octagon," and more, as well as his martial arts scenes with heavyweights of the genre, such as Jackie Chan and Chuck Norris. items.t: Trump tariffs hitting small business owners in multiple ways
items.x: WASHINGTON, D.C. (NEXSTAR) President Trump says his tariffs are helping the American economy grow but for some small businesses, the math isn't working out. From higher prices to fewer products on store shelves, one Virginia shop is finding ways to adapt. For Ben Knezic, running The Cut Butchery in Alexandria, Virginia – a Washington suburb – means offering customers a little bit of everything. From fresh meats and seafood to imported wines, cheeses and specialty foods, Knezic says Trump's tariffs are making some of those products more expensive. “Just seeing prices on our goods go up and up,” said Knezic. “We've had to raise prices on a lot of things like cheese and wine and some of the other stuff we import." items.x: KNOXVILLE, Tenn. (WATE) — Knox County criminal court Judge Scott Green spent much of his career working in the criminal justice system. First as a prosecutor, then as a defense attorney, and was eventually elected to the bench in 2014. Green died at age 64 on Friday, October 30 . Colleagues of Judge Green reminisced on his career and presence within the City County Building. Knox County District Attorney General Charme Allen spoke on his work and how he consistently had one underlying theme. "He was just a man who cared about people, and he wanted to do everything he could to help people and to make a difference in their lives and to make positive change," she said. Allen went on to explain that Green used his position to help people, whether defending, prosecuting, or presiding. Beyond the bench, Allen said that Green had a sense of humor. items.t: Ziploc and Cheerios are making cereal boxes that actually seal. Finally
items.x: ( SavorNation ) It’s genuinely baffling that it took until the end of 2026 to invent a cereal box that actually closes . For decades, we’ve all just accepted that opening cereal means wrestling with a flimsy plastic liner that immediately rips in half. After that, you’re just left to awkwardly roll the bag down and pray it doesn’t go stale by Tuesday. items.t: Up to 75% of NFL players who died had signs of CTE, new study says
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — As many as 75% of NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023 may have had chronic traumatic encephalopathy , better known as CTE, a new study from researchers at Boston University estimates. CTE is a "progressive neurodegenerative disease associated with exposure to repetitive head impacts, such as those from contact sport participation, military combat exposure, intimate partner violence, and other sources," according to the study. It is most frequently diagnosed in American football players. Researchers can identify the disease only after death, usually by examining donated brains. As a result, determining how many NFL players may have CTE has proven difficult. Most donations come from families whose loved ones had memory and behavior problems, two symptoms of the ailment, thus skewing results. items.x: SALT LAKE CITY ( ABC4 ) — The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints is set to donate $3 million to support the removal of invasive plant species around the Great Salt Lake. The Church has committed to donate the money to the Office of the Great Salt Lake Commissioner to speed up the removal of invasive phragmites, an extremely water-intensive species. Removing phragmites is part of critical habitat restoration, protecting shoreline wetlands, and helping make sure that water flows into the lake like it's supposed to. Phragmites (also known as common reed or by its scientific name Phragmites australis) is an aggressive reed that grows in dense stands up to 15 feet tall, consuming tens of thousands of acre-feet of water per year and degrading habitat needed by millions of migratory birds. items.t: Turn this on to stop hackers from stealing your phone number
items.x: ( KTLA ) – Your phone number is more valuable than you might think. It doesn’t just let people call or text you. It can also be the key to getting into your bank accounts, email and other important services. That’s because so many companies still send two-factor authentication codes by text message. If a hacker takes control of your phone number, they could potentially intercept those codes and use them to break into your accounts, KTLA tech reporter Rich DeMuro explains. The attack is called SIM swapping. It happens when someone tricks your wireless carrier into transferring your phone number to a SIM card or eSIM they control. AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon all offer free security features designed to help prevent this. The catch? You typically have to turn them on yourself. Here’s exactly how to do it. items.x: ( NewsNation ) — As many as 75% of NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023 may have had chronic traumatic encephalopathy , better known as CTE, a new study from researchers at Boston University estimates. CTE is a "progressive neurodegenerative disease associated with exposure to repetitive head impacts, such as those from contact sport participation, military combat exposure, intimate partner violence, and other sources," according to the study. It is most frequently diagnosed in American football players. Researchers can identify the disease only after death, usually by examining donated brains. As a result, determining how many NFL players may have CTE has proven difficult. Most donations come from families whose loved ones had memory and behavior problems, two symptoms of the ailment, thus skewing results. items.x: ( KTLA ) – Your phone number is more valuable than you might think. It doesn’t just let people call or text you. It can also be the key to getting into your bank accounts, email and other important services. That’s because so many companies still send two-factor authentication codes by text message. If a hacker takes control of your phone number, they could potentially intercept those codes and use them to break into your accounts, KTLA tech reporter Rich DeMuro explains. The attack is called SIM swapping. It happens when someone tricks your wireless carrier into transferring your phone number to a SIM card or eSIM they control. AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon all offer free security features designed to help prevent this. The catch? You typically have to turn them on yourself. Here’s exactly how to do it. items.t: Up to 75% of NFL players who died had signs of CTE, new study says
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — As many as 75% of NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023 may have had chronic traumatic encephalopathy , better known as CTE, a new study from researchers at Boston University estimates. CTE is a "progressive neurodegenerative disease associated with exposure to repetitive head impacts, such as those from contact sport participation, military combat exposure, intimate partner violence, and other sources," according to the study. It is most frequently diagnosed in American football players. Researchers can identify the disease only after death, usually by examining donated brains. As a result, determining how many NFL players may have CTE has proven difficult. Most donations come from families whose loved ones had memory and behavior problems, two symptoms of the ailment, thus skewing results. items.t: GM settles $220M lawsuit for allegedly selling private driver data
items.x: HARTFORD, Conn. ( WTNH ) — General Motors has agreed to pay $220 million to settle claims that it illegally sold drivers' private data and location information to third parties. The settlement, announced Thursday, concerns allegations that GM had sold the information to data brokers, who in turn sold it to insurance companies. That private data, in part, was then used to set insurance rates, according to a coalition of attorneys general in 35 states and Washington D.C. “GM turned private vehicles into mobile insurance surveillance machines without consumer consent or awareness," Connecticut Attorney General William Tong said in a Thursday press release announcing the settlement. "GM profited from the sale of this personal driving data, and consumers paid the price in the form of higher premiums." items.t: Turn this on to stop hackers from stealing your phone number
items.x: ( KTLA ) – Your phone number is more valuable than you might think. It doesn’t just let people call or text you. It can also be the key to getting into your bank accounts, email and other important services. That’s because so many companies still send two-factor authentication codes by text message. If a hacker takes control of your phone number, they could potentially intercept those codes and use them to break into your accounts, KTLA tech reporter Rich DeMuro explains. The attack is called SIM swapping. It happens when someone tricks your wireless carrier into transferring your phone number to a SIM card or eSIM they control. AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon all offer free security features designed to help prevent this. The catch? You typically have to turn them on yourself. Here’s exactly how to do it. items.t: Turn this on to stop hackers from stealing your phone number
items.x: ( KTLA ) – Your phone number is more valuable than you might think. It doesn’t just let people call or text you. It can also be the key to getting into your bank accounts, email and other important services. That’s because so many companies still send two-factor authentication codes by text message. If a hacker takes control of your phone number, they could potentially intercept those codes and use them to break into your accounts, KTLA tech reporter Rich DeMuro explains. The attack is called SIM swapping. It happens when someone tricks your wireless carrier into transferring your phone number to a SIM card or eSIM they control. AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon all offer free security features designed to help prevent this. The catch? You typically have to turn them on yourself. Here’s exactly how to do it. (WRIC) The Virginia NAACP says Virginians should know their rights if they encounter a Department of Justice election monitor on Election Day. “You are not required to stop, to stay, or to answer questions,” said Anthony Ashton, Senior Associate General Counsel, Office of General Counsel, National NAACP. Earlier this week, a Department of Justice spokesperson said observers will be in all 50 states, including Virginia. The spokesperson said monitors are there to observe and report any potential law violations, not to interfere. The NAACP said neutral election monitors, whether from the DOJ or not, should not speak to you before you have voted. “Anything that might be seen as discouraging or intimidating people with regard to voting, it would be illegal, and it doesn’t matter who does it,” Ashton said. items.t: Death of ‘Mad Max’ actor Richard Norton linked to peptides, coroner says
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — The death of Australian actor Richard Norton has been linked to injecting unapproved peptides , according to a new coroner's report. Norton, 75, went into cardiac arrest in March 2025 after injecting prescribed but unapproved CJC1295 and ipamorelin, according to multiple reports . "Richard's death was triggered by his injection of the peptide CJC1295/Ipamorelin," the report reads. "Richard had been taking amounts of the medication in excess of the dose prescribed by his medical practitioner. The injection caused an anaphylactic reaction which in turn led to cardiac arrest." Norton was known for his role in "Mad Max: Fury Road," "The Octagon," and more, as well as his martial arts scenes with heavyweights of the genre, such as Jackie Chan and Chuck Norris. items.x: WASHINGTON, D.C. (NEXSTAR) President Trump says his tariffs are helping the American economy grow but for some small businesses, the math isn't working out. From higher prices to fewer products on store shelves, one Virginia shop is finding ways to adapt. For Ben Knezic, running The Cut Butchery in Alexandria, Virginia – a Washington suburb – means offering customers a little bit of everything. From fresh meats and seafood to imported wines, cheeses and specialty foods, Knezic says Trump's tariffs are making some of those products more expensive. “Just seeing prices on our goods go up and up,” said Knezic. “We've had to raise prices on a lot of things like cheese and wine and some of the other stuff we import." items.t: Christa Pike says she remains in constant pain after botched execution in Tennessee
items.x: NASHVILLE, Tenn. ( WKRN ) — A month after Tennessee failed to execute the only woman on death row, Christa Pike has released a statement through her attorneys. Pike, 50, said she had been "prepared to die" when she entered the execution chamber at a Tennessee prison last month. Then, after surviving the failed execution by lethal injection, she said she "woke up alone in a hospital confused and in pain." "There hasn’t been a moment since that night when I haven’t been in pain. My body hurts. My arms hurt," Pike said in the statement. "My hands hurt. My throat hurts. I still struggle to speak. And the pain isn’t just physical. There is pain in my mind and in my soul." Doctors on Pike's legal team suggest the IV line was not placed properly, causing the lethal injection drugs to enter surrounding tissue rather than her bloodstream. items.t: Leo XIV becomes first pope ever to vote in US general election
items.x: VATICAN CITY (AP) — Pope Leo XIV has become the first pope to vote in a U.S. general election. The Vatican confirmed Friday that the Chicago-born pontiff had submitted a mail-in ballot in Chicago ahead of November’s midterm elections, citing his long-standing belief in civic participation. Leo, formerly Robert Prevost, “has exercised his right to vote as a United States citizen” and has done so “whenever he was eligible to do so,” the Holy See press office said. The statement said he had also voted while living in Peru whenever he was eligible. “The Holy Father expresses his belief in the right and the duty of citizens to participate in democratic processes,” it added. Leo’s vote was first reported by the Chicago Sun-Times, which quoted the chief of staff at the Will County clerk’s office as saying the pope, registered at a New Lenox address, requested a mail-in ballot on Oct. 3. items.t: Up to 75% of NFL players who died had signs of CTE, new study says
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — As many as 75% of NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023 may have had chronic traumatic encephalopathy , better known as CTE, a new study from researchers at Boston University estimates. CTE is a "progressive neurodegenerative disease associated with exposure to repetitive head impacts, such as those from contact sport participation, military combat exposure, intimate partner violence, and other sources," according to the study. It is most frequently diagnosed in American football players. Researchers can identify the disease only after death, usually by examining donated brains. As a result, determining how many NFL players may have CTE has proven difficult. Most donations come from families whose loved ones had memory and behavior problems, two symptoms of the ailment, thus skewing results. For decades, we’ve all just accepted that opening cereal means wrestling with a flimsy plastic liner that immediately rips in half. Instead of the usual cheap plastic liner that tears immediately, the box now has a resealable Ziploc bag built in to lock in freshness. items.t: York Sheriff’s Office introduces new tool to help check on seniors
items.x: YORK COUNTY, Va. (WAVY) The York County Sheriff's office has introduced a new tool to help with wellness checks for seniors. The tool, called ConfirmOK, is designed to give seniors added security and peace of mind. Participants receive an automated phone call each day at a specific time at their choosing to make sure they are safe. If the call isn't answered, additional steps are taken to make sure the person is ok. The Sheriff says in a video that there is no equipment to install, no app to download, and no hardware for residents to manage. Residents who are interested in this program should call 757-890-3639.

The State of North Carolina is providing an additional $258,000 for the project, requiring no funding from Dare County. The grant allocation follows ongoing beach erosion along the Outer Banks that has repeatedly damaged coastal structures. According to the National Park Service, 32 privately-owned homes have collapsed on Cape Hatteras National Seashore beaches since 2020. items.t: Dangerous amoeba in Louisiana tap water infects 10 people
items.x: NEW ORLEANS ( WGNO ) — In the last two years, 10 Louisianians were infected by an amoeba that the Louisiana Department of Health (LDH) said can be found in ordinary tap water. According to LDH officials, "Acanthamoeba" is commonly found in "soil, dust and water, including tap water." Seven of the patients infected by the amoeba were contact lens-wearers, who were infected when they used tap water to rinse the lenses. Five of those seven patients suffered permanent vision loss. Wetter winter anticipated because of El Niño Additionally, LDH officials report that two other patients were infected when they rinsed their sinuses, using tap water in a neti pot or a similar device. LDH Epidemiologist Theresa Sokol said that proper hygiene, for both contact lens cleaning and nasal rinsing, involves only distilled, sterile, or boiled water. items.t: Trump tariffs hitting small business owners in multiple ways
items.x: WASHINGTON, D.C. (NEXSTAR) President Trump says his tariffs are helping the American economy grow but for some small businesses, the math isn't working out. From higher prices to fewer products on store shelves, one Virginia shop is finding ways to adapt. For Ben Knezic, running The Cut Butchery in Alexandria, Virginia – a Washington suburb – means offering customers a little bit of everything. From fresh meats and seafood to imported wines, cheeses and specialty foods, Knezic says Trump's tariffs are making some of those products more expensive. “Just seeing prices on our goods go up and up,” said Knezic. “We've had to raise prices on a lot of things like cheese and wine and some of the other stuff we import." The shop opened just last year and is already having to rethink what it can sell. He says some imported wines now cost 10% more – with those higher costs passed on to customers. M

items.t: Death of ‘Mad Max’ actor Richard Norton linked to peptides, coroner says
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — The death of Australian actor Richard Norton has been linked to injecting unapproved peptides , according to a new coroner's report. Norton, 75, went into cardiac arrest in March 2025 after injecting prescribed but unapproved CJC1295 and ipamorelin, according to multiple reports . "Richard's death was triggered by his injection of the peptide CJC1295/Ipamorelin," the report reads. "Richard had been taking amounts of the medication in excess of the dose prescribed by his medical practitioner. The injection caused an anaphylactic reaction which in turn led to cardiac arrest." Norton was known for his role in "Mad Max: Fury Road," "The Octagon," and more, as well as his martial arts scenes with heavyweights of the genre, such as Jackie Chan and Chuck Norris. items.x: SLIDELL, La. ( WGNO ) – As meteorologists look ahead to the winter months, the presence of a strong El Niño in the Pacific is expected to make its mark here in the New Orleans area. "Typically, with El Niño, there is a wetter winter, and near normal, to maybe slightly below normal temperatures," Christopher Bannan, National Weather Service meteorologist, said. As for the possibility of below normal temperatures, they said that doesn't necessarily mean we should expect winter weather events like we have seen in years past. "Because a lot that's not necessarily meaning that a big arctic cold front would come down here," Bannan said. "It's more than we have a lot more rain, and a lot more cloud cover. items.t: Turn this on to stop hackers from stealing your phone number
items.x: ( KTLA ) – Your phone number is more valuable than you might think. It doesn’t just let people call or text you. It can also be the key to getting into your bank accounts, email and other important services. That’s because so many companies still send two-factor authentication codes by text message. If a hacker takes control of your phone number, they could potentially intercept those codes and use them to break into your accounts, KTLA tech reporter Rich DeMuro explains. The attack is called SIM swapping. It happens when someone tricks your wireless carrier into transferring your phone number to a SIM card or eSIM they control. AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon all offer free security features designed to help prevent this. The catch? You typically have to turn them on yourself. Here’s exactly how to do it. items.x: VATICAN CITY (AP) — Pope Leo XIV has become the first pope to vote in a U.S. general election. items.t: Turn this on to stop hackers from stealing your phone number
items.x: ( KTLA ) – Your phone number is more valuable than you might think. It doesn’t just let people call or text you. It can also be the key to getting into your bank accounts, email and other important services. That’s because so many companies still send two-factor authentication codes by text message. If a hacker takes control of your phone number, they could potentially intercept those codes and use them to break into your accounts, KTLA tech reporter Rich DeMuro explains. The attack is called SIM swapping. It happens when someone tricks your wireless carrier into transferring your phone number to a SIM card or eSIM they control. AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon all offer free security features designed to help prevent this. The catch? You typically have to turn them on yourself. Here’s exactly how to do it. items.t: Up to 75% of NFL players who died had signs of CTE, new study says
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — As many as 75% of NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023 may have had chronic traumatic encephalopathy , better known as CTE, a new study from researchers at Boston University estimates. CTE is a "progressive neurodegenerative disease associated with exposure to repetitive head impacts, such as those from contact sport participation, military combat exposure, intimate partner violence, and other sources," according to the study. It is most frequently diagnosed in American football players. Researchers can identify the disease only after death, usually by examining donated brains. As a result, determining how many NFL players may have CTE has proven difficult. Most donations come from families whose loved ones had memory and behavior problems, two symptoms of the ailment, thus skewing results. items.t: GM settles $220M lawsuit for allegedly selling private driver data
items.x: HARTFORD, Conn. ( WTNH ) — General Motors has agreed to pay $220 million to settle claims that it illegally sold drivers' private data and location information to third parties. The settlement, announced Thursday, concerns allegations that GM had sold the information to data brokers, who in turn sold it to insurance companies. That private data, in part, was then used to set insurance rates, according to a coalition of attorneys general in 35 states and Washington D.C. “GM turned private vehicles into mobile insurance surveillance machines without consumer consent or awareness," Connecticut Attorney General William Tong said in a Thursday press release announcing the settlement. "GM profited from the sale of this personal driving data, and consumers paid the price in the form of higher premiums." items.t: After 65 years, Freedom Riders finally complete their journey to New Orleans
items.x: Multiple generations of Black civil rights activists met at Xavier University on Wednesday to honor a group of Freedom Riders after they finally completed a disrupted bus journey from Washington D.C. to New Orleans 65 years after the original trip was halted. The original ride, the first in a series of trips to protest Jim Crow laws, was interrupted when a segregationist mob firebombed their buses in Anniston, Alabama on May 14, 1961. The 13 riders were able to escape the bus before it exploded but sustained beatings from the mob. The next day, they flew directly to New Orleans and sought refuge at Xavier University after hotels refused to host them out of fears of further violence. Leaving D.C. on Oct. 17 and stopping in historical cities like Selma and Jackson, the latest cohort of Freedom Riders completed the bus route their predecessors were unable to. items.x: ( NewsNation ) — The death of Australian actor Richard Norton has been linked to injecting unapproved peptides , according to a new coroner's report. Norton, 75, went into cardiac arrest in March 2025 after injecting prescribed but unapproved CJC1295 and ipamorelin, according to multiple reports . "Richard's death was triggered by his injection of the peptide CJC1295/Ipamorelin," the report reads. "Richard had been taking amounts of the medication in excess of the dose prescribed by his medical practitioner. The injection caused an anaphylactic reaction which in turn led to cardiac arrest." Norton was known for his role in "Mad Max: Fury Road," "The Octagon," and more, as well as his martial arts scenes with heavyweights of the genre, such as Jackie Chan and Chuck Norris. items.t: Turn this on to stop hackers from stealing your phone number
items.x: ( KTLA ) – Your phone number is more valuable than you might think. It doesn’t just let people call or text you. It can also be the key to getting into your bank accounts, email and other important services. That’s because so many companies still send two-factor authentication codes by text message. If a hacker takes control of your phone number, they could potentially intercept those codes and use them to break into your accounts, KTLA tech reporter Rich DeMuro explains. The attack is called SIM swapping. It happens when someone tricks your wireless carrier into transferring your phone number to a SIM card or eSIM they control. AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon all offer free security features designed to help prevent this. The catch? You typically have to turn them on yourself. Here’s exactly how to do it. items.t: Daycare workers charged in death of Winter Jones in court
items.x: MEMPHIS, Tenn. Two of the three daycare workers indicted in the death of 6-year-old Winter Jones , who died after being left inside a daycare van in August, were due back in court on Friday morning. The bus driver Tametria Norry, assistant director Sabrina Powe, and daycare assistant Amilya Hardin are all charged with aggravated child neglect, criminally negligent homicide, and destruction of or tampering with governmental records. Norry and Powe were scheduled for a hearing Friday morning, while the judge excused Hardin, who attends college full-time in Shelby County. However, neither of the three appeared. Instead, the state asked for additional time to get the new discovery in the case completed. At the end of the hearing, Norry's attorney asked that the court allow her client to apply for another job focused in social services where she would work inside a rehab facility as a cook. "

items.t: Diaper drive planned in Senatobia to honor Kohen Wiley
items.x: MEMPHIS, Tenn. This weekend will mark what would have been the second birthday of baby Kohen Wiley, who was killed when Senatobia police fired on a car in the parking lot of a Walmart. His death quickly made national headlines, as word spread beyond the Mid-South that it all started because kohen's mom and aunt allegedly left the Walmart without paying for a box of Pampers. So'nya Jones, with Healing Voices Network, was one of those watching in disbelief. "It took me, because I'm like, that's a one-year-old, shot, murdered over an alleged box of pampers," Jones noted. She not only watched, but she was spurred to action, even though she lives miles away in Wilmington, Delaware. She wanted to do something to bring awareness and help families who needed support in getting items for their kids. "So I reached out to a few people and said, hey, you know, I want to do a Pampers and wipes drive.

On October 21, Danielle Sturgeon was working at the Chick-fil-A in Jonesboro, Arkansas, when she heard a commotion at a table and saw a man holding a little girl upside down. Sturgeon ran over to the table, realized the 1-year-old was choking, and began patting her back and praying. She said the little girl was already turning blue. "I was like, Jesus, please, like, tell me what to do," said Sturgeon. Sturgeon heard a woman say someone needed to do the Heimlich maneuver and said nobody moved. items.t: Christa Pike says she remains in constant pain after botched execution in Tennessee
items.x: NASHVILLE, Tenn. ( WKRN ) — A month after Tennessee failed to execute the only woman on death row, Christa Pike has released a statement through her attorneys. Pike, 50, said she had been "prepared to die" when she entered the execution chamber at a Tennessee prison last month. Then, after surviving the failed execution by lethal injection, she said she "woke up alone in a hospital confused and in pain." "There hasn’t been a moment since that night when I haven’t been in pain. My body hurts. My arms hurt," Pike said in the statement. "My hands hurt. My throat hurts. I still struggle to speak. And the pain isn’t just physical. There is pain in my mind and in my soul." Doctors on Pike's legal team suggest the IV line was not placed properly, causing the lethal injection drugs to enter surrounding tissue rather than her bloodstream. items.x: VATICAN CITY (AP) — Pope Leo XIV has become the first pope to vote in a U.S. general election. The Vatican confirmed Friday that the Chicago-born pontiff had submitted a mail-in ballot in Chicago ahead of November’s midterm elections, citing his long-standing belief in civic participation. Leo, formerly Robert Prevost, “has exercised his right to vote as a United States citizen” and has done so “whenever he was eligible to do so,” the Holy See press office said. The statement said he had also voted while living in Peru whenever he was eligible. “The Holy Father expresses his belief in the right and the duty of citizens to participate in democratic processes,” it added. The exchange, which described the situation as a "security issue," has temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals while it "conducts security checks, freezes funds, and works with law enforcement." It vowed to cover all losses. "It does look like a hack on Binance," the company's co-founder Changpeng Zhao wrote in a post on the social platform X. He touted fellow crypto firms Tether and Circle for quickly freezing funds. Zhao acknowledged he no longer manages the company but said he expects "all user funds will be fully covered." The Binance co-founder stepped down as CEO in 2023 when he pleaded guilty to violating anti-money laundering laws. President Trump pardoned Zhao in November 2025. items.t: Up to 75% of NFL players who died had signs of CTE, new study says
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — As many as 75% of NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023 may have had chronic traumatic encephalopathy , better known as CTE, a new study from researchers at Boston University estimates. CTE is a "progressive neurodegenerative disease associated with exposure to repetitive head impacts, such as those from contact sport participation, military combat exposure, intimate partner violence, and other sources," according to the study. It is most frequently diagnosed in American football players. Researchers can identify the disease only after death, usually by examining donated brains. As a result, determining how many NFL players may have CTE has proven difficult. Most donations come from families whose loved ones had memory and behavior problems, two symptoms of the ailment, thus skewing results. items.t: Copiah County sees uptick in fires amid dry conditions
items.x: COPIAH COUNTY, Miss. ( WJTV ) Copiah County emergency responders are on high alert after a surge in grass fires this month. Crews have responded to more than 170 fires in October alone, putting a strain on both firefighters and county resources. "Our numbers have exceeded everybody that I've talked to. As of date this month, we've had 171 grass fires, 63 rekindles and two losses of homes associated with grass fires today," said Darryl Hilliard, director of the Copiah County Emergency Management Agency. Hilliard said the number of grass fires this month is more than double what the county saw during the same period last year. He said many of the fires were connected to human activity, prompting another plea for people to follow the county's burn ban. items.x: NEW YORK (AP) — A historic drop for Alphabet’s stock dragged the U.S. market lower Thursday after the company behind Google and YouTube reported weaker growth for the summer than analysts expected. Alphabet is one of the most influential stocks on Wall Street because it’s one of the largest, and the Class A shares of its stock fell 12.6% for their worst day since they began trading more than 20 years ago. items.t: GM settles $220M lawsuit for allegedly selling private driver data
items.x: HARTFORD, Conn. ( WTNH ) — General Motors has agreed to pay $220 million to settle claims that it illegally sold drivers' private data and location information to third parties. The settlement, announced Thursday, concerns allegations that GM had sold the information to data brokers, who in turn sold it to insurance companies. That private data, in part, was then used to set insurance rates, according to a coalition of attorneys general in 35 states and Washington D.C. “GM turned private vehicles into mobile insurance surveillance machines without consumer consent or awareness," Connecticut Attorney General William Tong said in a Thursday press release announcing the settlement. "GM profited from the sale of this personal driving data, and consumers paid the price in the form of higher premiums." GM's settlement resolves claims in 35 states and Washington, D.C.
